front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** operates its Community Living – Group Home service in Maryland. The service is delivered under the DDA Community Pathways Waiver and licensed as a community residential service under COMAR Title 10, Subtitle 22.

The manual is meant to:

- Put in writing the policies and procedures that **COMAR 10.22.02.10** requires of a licensee. These cover health and safety, fundamental rights, choice, confidentiality, grievances, incident reporting, medication administration, behavior safeguards, finances, infection control and emergency/evacuation planning.
- Give every staff member, care provider, consultant and volunteer one reference for what the agency expects. Under COMAR 10.22.02.10C, all of them must know and implement every policy.
- Support the people we serve in their homes, including their rights, choices, health and safety, and the services in their Individual Plans (IP) and person-centered plans.
- Help the agency prepare for licensure surveys, complaint investigations and Medicaid/waiver oversight by OHCQ, DDA and other regulators.
- Show how the governing body, administrative head and staff share responsibility for compliance.

This manual is a compliance and operations tool. It does not replace the regulations, the approved Program Service Plan (PSP), the approved Quality Assurance plan, or advice from legal counsel. If this manual conflicts with a regulation or a DDA/OHCQ directive, the regulation or directive controls.

## How to Use This Manual

### 1. Customize it before use
This is a **template**. Before it is used, **[AGENCY NAME]** must tailor every section to its own operations. Replace every placeholder, including **[AGENCY NAME]**, **[ADMINISTRATIVE HEAD / TITLE]**, **[GOVERNING BODY NAME]**, **[SITE ADDRESSES]**, **[LICENSED CAPACITY]**, **[REGIONAL OFFICE CONTACT]** and **[EFFECTIVE DATE]**. Align the content with the agency's:

- Approved Program Service Plan (COMAR 10.22.02.09)
- DDA-approved Quality Assurance plan (COMAR 10.22.02.14)
- Staffing plan (COMAR 10.22.02.11A)
- Site-specific emergency plan (COMAR 10.22.02.10B)
- Licensed capacity and sites (COMAR 10.22.02.06)

Delete or revise any language that does not fit how the agency actually works. A policy that is not followed in practice is itself a compliance risk.

### 2. Adopt it through the governing body
The governing body is legally responsible for overseeing all programs and for compliance (COMAR 10.22.02.02A(2)-(3)). Its bylaws must cover policy approval, conflict of interest and responses to plans of correction (COMAR 10.22.02.08). Present the customized manual to **[GOVERNING BODY NAME]** for review and formal adoption. Record the adoption date, the vote and the version number in the minutes, and note them on the manual's cover or revision page.

### 3. Keep it current
Review the manual on a set schedule, at least annually and whenever any of the following occurs:

- A regulation, waiver provision, DDA/OHCQ guidance or billing/rate rule changes. Examples are an amended COMAR chapter, a CMS-approved waiver amendment, or an updated DDA form.
- A survey, complaint investigation or plan of correction identifies a gap.
- The agency opens, closes or relocates a site, changes its licensed capacity, or revises its PSP or QA plan.
- An incident, trend or QA committee review shows a policy needs improving.

Record each revision with its date, what changed, and the governing body's approval. Keep superseded versions on file. Check the current text of each cited regulation on the official source before relying on this manual. Items in the regulatory framework that were taken from prior research and not re-fetched for this edition are marked "verify current text" below.

### 4. Train staff on it
Staff must be trained on the policies that apply to their work. Do this at orientation and again when policies change.

- Train employees, care providers, consultants and volunteers before they perform independent duties, as required by COMAR 10.22.02.11C-D and COMAR 10.22.08.04B.
- Document who was trained, on what, and when. DDA's Staff Training Form DD.APP.1.1 is available for the COMAR 10.22.02.11C and D topics.
- Keep signed acknowledgments that each person has received, read and understood the manual, and keep them in personnel records.
- Give each person served, and their proponent, enough information about the grievance process to use it (COMAR 10.22.02.10D).

### 5. Navigating the manual
Each policy section should state the requirement and its regulatory source, who is responsible, the step-by-step procedure, what must be documented, and when to notify OHCQ, DDA or others. Cross-reference the regulatory citations in the next section, and use the emergency-plan and records provisions at the site level.

## Regulatory Framework

The rules below are the sources this manual draws on, listed by their exact citation text. Summaries are drawn from the cited provisions and are not a substitute for reading the full text. Items marked *(verify current text)* were taken from prior research and not re-fetched when this front matter was prepared.

### A. Maryland licensing regulations (COMAR 10.22.02, Administrative Requirements for Licensees)

| Citation | Subject and key points |
|---|---|
| **COMAR 10.22.02** | Chapter 02, Administrative Requirements for Licensees (.01-1 through .14). Authority: Health-General §§7-904 and 7-909. |
| **COMAR 10.22.02.01-1** | License Required. A license is required to provide community residential services. *(verify current text)* |
| **COMAR 10.22.02.02** | Application for Initial License or Renewal. Corporate status and governing body responsibility; application contents; renewal filed at least 60 days before expiration; Director's decision options; voluntary surrender with a closure schedule submitted at least 90 days ahead; termination of services to an individual only for good cause with the Director's written approval, 90 days' written notice and notice of hearing rights under COMAR 10.22.16. |
| **COMAR 10.22.02.03** | Investigation by the Administration. Sets OHCQ investigation priorities; Priority 1 (immediate jeopardy) investigations start within 2 working days. *(verify current text)* The plan-of-correction deadline is in .04E, not .03. |
| **COMAR 10.22.02.04** | Compliance Monitoring. OHCQ monitoring; pre-licensure survey; announced and unannounced visits at least annually; complaint investigation visits; plan of correction due at the exit conference or within 10 working days of receiving findings (OHCQ may require it sooner; the OHCQ Director may grant an extension of up to 30 days); revised plan of correction within 10 working days if the first is unacceptable. |
| **COMAR 10.22.02.05** | New Site, Site Closure, or Relocation. DDA approval required at least 30 days in advance. *(verify current text)* |
| **COMAR 10.22.02.06** | Licensed Capacity. The license states the number of people that may be served; exceeding it requires Director approval, for a maximum of 60 days plus one 60-day extension. *(verify current text)* |
| **COMAR 10.22.02.08** | Governing Body. Required membership, residency, no employee voting members, and required bylaw content. Board members and employees may not own property leased back to the licensee (.08C(9)). *(verify current text)* |
| **COMAR 10.22.02.09** | Program Service Plan (PSP). Required for each service; DDA approval of revisions before implementation; governing body review at least every 3 years; compliance with the approved PSP. |
| **COMAR 10.22.02.10** | Policies and Procedures. Written policies on the topics in A(1)-(19); site emergency plan requirements in B; all staff, care providers, consultants and volunteers must know and implement every policy (C); grievance process information for individuals and proponents (D). |
| **COMAR 10.22.02.11** | Staffing Requirements. Staffing plan; criminal history screening; training before independent duties and within 3 months of hire; job descriptions and nondiscrimination policy. |
| **COMAR 10.22.02.12** | Health and Safety Requirements. Zoning, building and life-safety codes; fire safety; water temperature; medication administration and packaging. |
| **COMAR 10.22.02.13** | Records. Site-based records, minimum contents, emergency access, 6-year retention, and electronic record requirements including HIPAA compliance and off-site backup. |
| **COMAR 10.22.02.14** | Quality Assurance. DDA-approved QA plan; internal QA system; standing committee review of incidents, restrictive behavior plans and rights restrictions. |

### B. Maryland community residential services regulations

| Citation | Subject and key points |
|---|---|
| **COMAR 10.22.08.03** | Scope (Community Residential Services). Defines the scope of community residential services. *(verify current text)* |
| **COMAR 10.22.08.04** | Staffing and Training (Community Residential Services). Staffing levels and patterns as determined in the IP; training per COMAR 10.22.02.11. |

Cross-references found within the provisions above, which should be consulted directly when drafting the related policies: Health-General §§7-603, 7-1002, 7-1010, 5-605 and 19-1902 et seq.; COMAR 10.22.05 (IP); COMAR 10.22.16 (hearing rights); COMAR 10.27.11; and COMAR 12.15.03.

### C. Medicaid waiver and federal requirements

| Citation | Subject and key points |
|---|---|
| **Community Pathways Waiver, Appendix C — Community Living – Group Home** | Service definition, residence requirements and provider standards. Includes the maximum of 4 participants per residence unless previously approved by DDA, private bedrooms, 24/7 availability with back-up support, staff qualifications, Medication Technician and RN delegation rules, transportation in the daily rate, room and board collected from the resident, up to 18 retainer days per person per year, and the prohibition on payment to relatives, legal guardians or legally responsible persons. |
| **Community Pathways Waiver, Appendix I** | Financial accountability. Bill only services authorized in the approved PCP and Detailed Service Authorization in LTSSMaryland; room and board are excluded from the rate. |
| **42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)** | HCBS settings requirements for provider-owned or controlled residential settings: lease or equivalent agreement, privacy, lockable doors, roommate choice, and access to food and visitors. |
| **42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi)** | Additional requirements for provider-owned or controlled residential settings. Any modification of these conditions must be supported by a specific assessed need and documented in the person-centered plan. |
| **DDA Addendum for Participation in Maryland Medical Assistance Program — PT 90 DDA** | Each licensed site needs its own "DDA Licensed Site MA" number. Enrollment, revalidation and SDAT good-standing checks run through MPRIME; losing SDAT good standing causes immediate suspension. |
| **Provider Portal Residential Services 2023 Billing Update (Jan 27, 2023)** | "Number of People Authorized" (people living in the home and present, or on retainer days, max 18 per year) drives the residential billing rate. |
| **DDA Addendum for Licensed Services and Sites (MDH Form DD.ADD.1.0, 06.02.2022)** | Site addendum listing each site, capacity requested and proposed occupancy date, with the Community Settings Rule attestation. |
| **DDA New Site Visit Checklist (Community Settings Rule), Nov 14, 2022** | New-site inspection form covering institutional or isolating characteristics, heightened scrutiny and settings-rule items. |

### D. Workforce and employment requirements

| **Maryland Wage and Hour Law facts (MD Labor)** | State and local minimum wage. State minimum is $15.00/hr; Montgomery, Howard and Prince George's Counties have higher local rates. Confirm the rate for each site's county and the agency's size before setting wages. |

### E. Regulators and contacts

### F. Maintaining this framework

This list reflects the citations available when the manual was prepared. It may not cover every law that applies to **[AGENCY NAME]**, such as local ordinances, other employment laws or insurance requirements. Before adoption, have **[AGENCY NAME]** or its counsel confirm the current text of each regulation, add any rules specific to the agency's sites and operations, and recheck the list whenever the manual is reviewed. Phone numbers and web addresses should also be confirmed, since regulators change them.

citations.requirement: A license is required to provide community residential services. Taken from the fact-checked research; the text was not re-fetched.

citations.title: Application for Initial License or Renewal
citations.requirement: A.(1): the licensee must be a Maryland corporation, or a foreign corporation registered in MD. A.(2)-(3): the governing body is legally responsible for overseeing all programs and for compliance. A.(4): the application needs a business plan, a DD experience summary, prior licensing reports from the last 10 years, and a DDA-approved QA plan. B.: file renewal at least 60 days before the license expires. D.: the Director may approve, approve with conditions, deny, or request more information. F.: voluntary surrender needs a closure schedule submitted at least 90 days ahead and approved by the Director. G.: terminate services to an individual only for good cause with the Director's written approval. Give the Director 90 days' written notice, give the individual and proponent written notice of the right to a hearing under COMAR 10.22.16, and copy the regional office and team. Services are considered terminated after 60 consecutive days' absence unless the Director decides otherwise.

citations.title: Investigation by the Administration
citations.requirement: Sets OHCQ investigation priorities. Priority 1 (immediate jeopardy) investigations start within 2 working days. Taken from the fact-checked research. NOTE: the fetched text of .04E, not .03, contains the 10-working-day plan-of-correction rule; cite .04E for the POC deadline.

citations.title: Compliance Monitoring
citations.requirement: A.: OHCQ, as the Administration's agent, monitors and inspects licensees. B.: an on-site pre-licensure survey is required. C.: announced and unannounced licensure visits happen at least annually. D.: announced or unannounced complaint investigation visits. E.: submit a plan of correction (POC) at the exit conference or within 10 working days of receiving the findings. OHCQ may require it sooner, and the OHCQ Director may grant an extension of up to 30 days. F.: if a POC is unacceptable, resubmit a revised POC within 10 working days.

citations.title: New Site, Site Closure, or Relocation
citations.requirement: DDA approval is required at least 30 days in advance to open, close or relocate a site. Taken from the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Licensed Capacity
citations.requirement: The license states the number of people that may be served. Exceeding it requires Director approval, for a maximum of 60 days plus one 60-day extension. Taken from the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Governing Body
citations.requirement: Board membership must include at least 1 person with a DD, 1 family member of a person with a DD, and 1 person with DD experience. At least 75% of members must live in MD or within 100 miles. No employees or their immediate family may be voting members. Bylaws must cover oversight, compliance, mission/budget/policy approval, conflict of interest, POC responses and PSP approval. Board members and employees may not own property leased back to the licensee (.08C(9)). Taken from the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Program Service Plan (PSP)
citations.requirement: A.: a PSP is required for each service the licensee provides. B.: submit a revised PSP for DDA approval before implementing changes. C.: the administrative head ensures the governing body reviews and updates the PSP at least every 3 years. D.: comply with the approved PSP. E.: contents are rationale, scope, staffing and training, and setting and location (including the number of individuals expected to be served).

citations.title: Policies and Procedures
citations.requirement: A.(1)-(19) requires written policies on: health and safety per the IP; fundamental rights (Health-General §7-1002); promoting choice; confidentiality (Health-General §7-1010); a grievance process with anti-retaliation safeguards; nondiscrimination; reporting and investigating all incidents under DDA procedures; medication administration per DDA's curriculum; compliance with COMAR 10.27.11; behavior safeguards; property-damage payment; Health-General §5-605; no conflict of interest; GAAP fiscal practices; protection of individuals' finances (A(15)(a)-(e)); infection control and standard precautions; a disaster and evacuation plan with sufficient drills; and no individual performing paid staff duties or non-household tasks (A(18)-(19)). B.: group homes need an emergency plan covering evacuation or 72-hour shelter-in-place, an annual practice drill coordinated with local emergency planners, an after-action report and improvement plan, ID with health information, family and DDA regional office notification, staff recall, continuity of operations, off-site data backup, sharing the plan with local emergency management, and an executive summary for families on request. C.: all staff, care providers, consultants and volunteers must know and implement every policy. D.: give each individual and proponent enough information about the grievance process to use it.

citations.title: Staffing Requirements
citations.requirement: A.: analyze the number of individuals and each person's needs, then develop and implement a staffing plan that meets health and safety needs and delivers the IP services. There is no fixed numeric ratio. B.: no employing or contracting with anyone whose criminal history indicates behavior potentially harmful to individuals (Health-General §19-1902 et seq.; COMAR 12.15.03). C.: before independent duties, staff need job training, DDA-approved training (seizure disorders, principles of behavior change, management of disruptive behaviors, medication administration, aging) and OSHA blood-borne pathogens training under 29 CFR 1910.1030. D.: within 3 months of hire, DDA-approved training on community integration, individual-directed planning, characteristics and needs, First Aid/CPR (American Red Cross or equivalent), fundamental rights, communicable diseases, supporting choice, and communication skills. E.: written job descriptions and a policy to prevent employment discrimination.

citations.title: Health and Safety Requirements
citations.requirement: A.: each home must meet local zoning (except as provided in Health-General §7-603), local and State building codes and life-safety requirements, be free of hazards, and be in good repair. B.: free of fire hazards, with adequate smoke detectors, working and updated fire extinguishers, and a written fire evacuation plan. C.: water temperature at a maximum of 110°F unless every resident can regulate it safely and this is documented in each IP. D.: administer medication per DDA's medication curriculum, use unit-dose packaging for oral solids unless the IP says otherwise, package medication for absent individuals separately, and request pharmacy-generated MARs, TARs and physician order forms.

citations.title: Records
citations.requirement: A.: keep each individual's records at the site where the person is served. B.: minimum contents are application identifying information, emergency contact, next of kin, physician, diagnosis, allergies, medication list, the IP (COMAR 10.22.05), documentation of IP implementation, and anything else DDA requires. C.: on a medical emergency, make the person's medical information readily accessible to emergency personnel. D.: keep records at least 6 years, even if the person leaves or dies. Keep current-service documents for as long as the person is served, and organize records for easy access. E.: electronic records must meet the chapter, comply with HIPAA privacy and security rules, and be backed up and stored off-site.

citations.title: Quality Assurance
citations.requirement: A.: submit the QA plan and any substantive changes to DDA for approval. B.: an internal QA system that is focused on individual choice, preference and satisfaction (with personal contact), has measurable outcomes, analyzes trends, responds promptly when health or safety is at risk, and tracks behavior-plan restrictive techniques (who, which technique, date/time, emergency vs. plan, effectiveness). C.: set goals and standards, keep records, and implement changes based on the data. E.: standing committee(s) must review the incident protocol and all incidents, approve all behavior plans that use restrictive techniques, review and set time frames for rights restrictions not related to challenging behavior, and review policies for protection of rights. The committee must have equal numbers of licensee staff and non-employees (individuals, proponents or community members). Members may not decide on incidents or behavior plans they were involved in. It meets as needed with a majority present and must ensure confidentiality under Health-General §7-1010.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Program Director Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: Governing body members, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], Program Director, all managers and supervisors
policies.purpose: To establish [AGENCY NAME]'s legal organization, the composition and duties of its governing body, and the responsibilities of the Program Director. These arrangements ensure that the community residential services program (Community Living – Group Home, Community Pathways Waiver) is overseen and operated in compliance with COMAR 10.22.02.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is organized as a Maryland corporation, or a foreign corporation registered to do business in Maryland, as required by COMAR 10.22.02.02A(1). Archived OHCQ guidance indicates DDA does not accept limited liability companies, so [AGENCY NAME] will not apply for or hold a license under an LLC structure. The governing body is legally responsible for oversight of all programs and for compliance with COMAR 10.22.02 (.02A(2)-(3)). Its membership, bylaws and conflict-of-interest rules follow COMAR 10.22.02.08. The Program Director ensures that every staff member, care provider, consultant and volunteer knows and implements each policy (.10C). Managers must have at least 5 years of developmental disabilities experience, consistent with the DDA application.

definitions.definition: The board of directors of [AGENCY NAME], which holds legal responsibility for oversight of all programs and for compliance with COMAR 10.22.02.
The Maryland corporation, or foreign corporation registered in Maryland, that holds the community residential services license.
The manager designated by the governing body to direct day-to-day operation of the licensed program and implementation of all policies.
A spouse, parent, child, sibling or other close relative of an employee, as defined in the bylaws. Immediate family of employees may not serve as voting board members.
Program Service Plan. The governing body approves it under the bylaws.

procedures: The incorporator or board secretary confirms that [AGENCY NAME] is a Maryland corporation or a registered foreign corporation. A copy of the charter and SDAT good-standing evidence is kept in the corporate records file.

The governing body adopts written bylaws. The bylaws must address oversight, compliance, approval of the mission, budget and policies, conflict of interest, responses to plans of correction (POCs) and approval of the PSP.

The board secretary maintains a membership roster showing, for each voting member, the residence address and whether the member is an employee or an immediate family member of an employee. The roster is reviewed at least annually and whenever a seat changes.

The board chair confirms that membership at all times includes at least one person with a developmental disability, at least one family member of a person with a developmental disability, and at least one person with developmental disabilities experience.
The board chair confirms that at least 75% of voting members live in Maryland or within 100 miles of the state. No employee and no immediate family member of an employee may serve as a voting member.

If a board vacancy would cause the composition to fall out of compliance, the chair notifies [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] within 5 business days. The board recruits a qualified replacement and records the plan in the minutes.

Each board member and employee signs an annual disclosure. No board member or employee may own property that is leased to [AGENCY NAME] (.08C(9)). Any such arrangement identified is reported to the board chair immediately and resolved before any lease is signed or renewed.

The governing body meets at least quarterly. It reviews licensure status, QA reports, incident trends, financial reports and survey results, and it approves the budget and policies. Minutes are kept and signed.
The governing body reviews and approves each POC response before it is submitted to OHCQ. It also approves the PSP and any substantive change to it.
The administrative head, or two officers of the corporation, sign all license applications and renewals (.02C). The board chair verifies the signatory authority in a board resolution.

The governing body appoints a Program Director and records the appointment in the minutes. Before appointment, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] verifies that the person has at least 5 years of developmental disabilities experience and keeps the verification in the personnel file.

The Program Director analyzes the number of individuals served and each person's needs to maintain the staffing plan required by COMAR 10.22.02.11A (see ST-01). The Program Director also ensures written job descriptions exist for every position (see ST-06).

The Program Director gives each new employee, care provider, consultant and volunteer access to the policy manual before independent duties. The Program Director obtains a signed acknowledgment that the person will implement every policy (see GOV-03).

The Program Director reports to the governing body at each regular meeting on census, staffing, incidents, rights restrictions, training compliance, billing compliance and the status of open corrective actions.
The Program Director ensures an administrator or designated manager is reachable by phone at all times and that staff know how to reach that person. The 24-hour contact list is posted at each site.

responsibilities.duty: Oversees all programs and compliance, approves the mission, budget, policies, POC responses and PSP, maintains required composition, and appoints and evaluates the Program Director.
Presides over meetings, verifies membership composition, collects conflict disclosures and signs applications as authorized.
Serves as administrative head, signs license applications and renewals as authorized, verifies manager qualifications and reports to the board.
Directs daily operations, ensures every staff member, care provider, consultant and volunteer knows and implements each policy, and maintains the staffing plan and job descriptions.
Know and implement the policies and report suspected non-compliance to the Program Director.

documentation: Articles of incorporation and SDAT good-standing evidence
Bylaws and amendments
Board membership roster with residency and employee/family status
Signed annual conflict-of-interest and property-ownership disclosures
Board minutes and resolutions, including appointment of the Program Director and approval of policies, the PSP and POCs
Manager experience verifications and job descriptions
Signed staff policy acknowledgments

policies.title: Licensure, Qualified Provider Approval and Medicaid Provider Agreements
policies.applies_to: Governing body, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], Program Director, billing and compliance staff
policies.purpose: To ensure [AGENCY NAME] holds and maintains every approval needed to provide Community Living – Group Home services, and that no service is provided or billed without them.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will not provide community residential services without a license (COMAR 10.22.02.01-1). Three linked approvals are required: DDA qualified-provider approval, an OHCQ-administered license under COMAR 10.22.02, and a separate Medicaid MA number for each licensed site under the DDA Addendum (PT 90 DDA). [AGENCY NAME] will meet the provider standard of at least 5 years of demonstrated developmental disabilities residential experience. It will keep all approvals current, will renew licenses on time, and will not employ or contract with any person or entity excluded from federal or state health care programs.

definitions.definition: A provider approved by DDA to deliver services under the Community Pathways Waiver.
The community residential services license required by COMAR 10.22.02.01-1, issued by the DDA Director with OHCQ as DDA's licensing and monitoring agent.
The Medicaid provider number issued for each licensed site under the PT 90 DDA addendum. A site may not bill without its own number.
The Maryland Medicaid provider enrollment, revalidation and verification system, including SDAT good-standing checks.
The HHS Office of Inspector General List of Excluded Individuals and Entities.

procedures: [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] maintains a licensure calendar showing, for each approval, the effective date, expiration or revalidation date and the responsible person. The calendar is reviewed monthly.

Before applying, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] confirms that the agency can document at least 5 years of developmental disabilities residential experience. The application includes a business plan, a developmental disabilities experience summary, licensing reports from the last 10 years and a DDA-approved QA plan (see GOV-04).
The administrative head, or two officers, sign the application. A copy of the full application as filed is kept in the licensure file.

[AGENCY NAME] does not admit any person or begin billing at any site until the license, DDA approval and the site's own MA number are all in place. [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] verifies this in writing for each new site (see GOV-08).
Within 30 days of DDA approval of the policies and procedures, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] sends the approved policies and procedures to OHCQ and files proof of transmittal.
The governing body signs the Provider Agreement to Conditions of Participation. The original is kept in the licensure file and a copy goes to the billing office.
[ADMINISTRATOR NAME] files each license renewal at least 60 days before the license expires (.02B). The renewal is filed earlier if a signatory will be unavailable.
[ADMINISTRATOR NAME] understands that the license does not expire until the Director acts and the time for judicial review has lapsed. Renewal is nonetheless never allowed to run to the last days.

When the Director approves with conditions, denies, or requests more information (.02D), [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] notifies the board chair within 2 business days and responds by the stated due date. Any denial notice carries a right to request a hearing from OAH within 30 days. [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] calendars that deadline on the day the denial is received.

The billing office checks MPRIME at least monthly for SDAT good standing, Medicaid enrollment status and revalidation due dates. A loss of SDAT good standing causes immediate Medicaid suspension, so any warning is escalated to [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] the same day.
[ADMINISTRATOR NAME] files the annual SDAT report and any required corporate filings on time and keeps the confirmations.

Before hire or engagement, and at least annually afterward, the compliance designee screens all owners, board members, managers, employees and contractors against the OIG LEIE and the Maryland sanctioned provider list. Results are printed or saved to the file with the date and the reviewer's initials.

Any person who appears on an exclusion list is removed immediately from any role involving Medicaid-funded services. [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] notifies the board chair and seeks legal advice about any required reporting or repayment.
Each licensed site displays or keeps available its license as required, and [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] keeps current copies of all licenses and MA number notices at the administrative office.
Any change in ownership, governing body structure, location or services that could affect the license is reported to DDA and OHCQ before it takes effect, following GOV-07 and GOV-08.

responsibilities.duty: Authorizes applications, signs the Provider Agreement and oversees that all approvals remain in force.
Files applications and renewals, tracks the licensure calendar, responds to DDA and OHCQ actions and ensures no unapproved service or billing occurs.
Monitors MPRIME status, performs exclusion screening and keeps the evidence.
Ensures services are delivered only at licensed and enrolled sites.

documentation: Application, license and renewal filings, with dates of submission
DDA qualified-provider approval notice
MA number notice for each licensed site
Signed Provider Agreement to Conditions of Participation
Licensure calendar
MPRIME status checks and SDAT good-standing confirmations
Proof of transmittal of policies and procedures to OHCQ
Exclusion screening results

policies.title: Policy Review, Document Control and Staff Awareness
policies.applies_to: Governing body, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], Program Director, standing committee, all staff, care providers, consultants and volunteers
policies.purpose: To keep [AGENCY NAME]'s written policies complete, current and approved, and to ensure everyone who works for or with the agency knows and implements them.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains written policies covering every topic required by COMAR 10.22.02.10A(1)-(19) and the emergency plan required by .10B. Policies are approved by the governing body, reviewed for protection of individuals' rights by the standing committee (.14E(1)(f)), version-controlled, and made available to all staff, care providers, consultants and volunteers, who must know and implement them (.10C). Each individual and proponent receives enough information about the grievance process to use it (.10D).

definitions.definition: The controlled set of [AGENCY NAME]'s policies and procedures, including the policies in this manual.
The current approved version of a policy, identified by policy ID, version number and effective date.
A table mapping each item in COMAR 10.22.02.10A(1)-(19), and the .10B emergency plan elements, to the policy ID that covers it.
A person who advocates for an individual, such as a family member, guardian or other representative chosen by the individual.

procedures: [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] maintains the policy manual with each policy showing its ID, title, version number, effective date, approval date and next review date.

[ADMINISTRATOR NAME] maintains a cross-reference table linking each COMAR 10.22.02.10A(1)-(19) item and each .10B emergency plan element to the policy ID that covers it. The table is checked for gaps whenever a policy is added, retired or revised.
The governing body approves each new policy and each substantive revision, and records the approval in its minutes (policy approval is a governing body duty under the bylaws, .08C).
The standing committee reviews policies and their implementation to ensure legal and human rights are protected (.14E(1)(f)). The committee's review is recorded in its minutes (see GOV-05).
Each policy is formally reviewed at least annually. The reviewer records the date, findings and any revisions, and the results go to the governing body.

Policies are also reviewed after any change in law, regulation, DDA guidance or waiver rules, after a survey finding, and after an incident review that identifies a policy gap. The Program Director starts that review within 10 business days of learning of the trigger.
Policies that must be approved by DDA, such as the QA plan and the PSP, are not implemented in changed form until DDA approves the change (see GOV-04 and GOV-07).

When a policy changes, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] replaces the controlled copy at every location where policies are kept, marks superseded versions as retired, and keeps archived versions for at least 6 years.

The Program Director gives each new employee, care provider, consultant and volunteer access to the policy manual before independent duties. Each person signs an acknowledgment that they have read and will implement the policies, and the acknowledgment is kept in the personnel or volunteer file.
When a policy changes, the Program Director informs all affected staff within 7 days, using a staff meeting, written notice or training. Staff sign the sign-in or notice to show awareness.
Supervisors check on observation visits and records reviews that staff are implementing policies. The Program Director corrects deviations immediately and documents retraining.

At admission, and annually, the Program Director or designee explains the grievance process to each individual and proponent in a way the person understands, and gives written information on it (see IR-03). The date and the person who explained it are documented in the individual's record.

A copy of the current policy manual is kept at each site and at the administrative office and is accessible to staff at all times, including overnight. Individuals and proponents may request a copy of policies that affect them.

responsibilities.duty: Approves policies and substantive revisions.
Maintains the manual, version control and cross-reference table, and schedules annual reviews.
Ensures staff awareness and implementation, obtains acknowledgments and informs staff of changes.
Reviews policies for protection of legal and human rights.

responsibilities.role: All staff, care providers, consultants and volunteers
responsibilities.duty: Read, know and implement every policy.

documentation: Policy manual with version and approval dates
COMAR 10.22.02.10 cross-reference table
Annual review records
Governing body and standing committee minutes
Signed staff, consultant and volunteer acknowledgments
Staff meeting sign-in sheets or notices of policy changes
Records of grievance process information given to individuals and proponents

policies.title: Quality Assurance Plan, Data Review and Mortality Review
policies.applies_to: Governing body, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], Program Director, standing committee, QA designee, all staff
policies.purpose: To operate an internal quality assurance system that is centered on the choices, preferences and satisfaction of the individuals served, uses measurable data to improve services and protects health and safety.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will have a DDA-approved written QA plan, as required for the license application (COMAR 10.22.02.02A(4)), and will submit the plan and any substantive change to DDA for approval before implementing it (.14A). The QA system will focus on individual choice, preference and satisfaction, with personal contact with the people served. It will use measurable goals, analyze trends, respond promptly when health or safety is at risk and track the use of restrictive techniques in behavior plans (.14B). [AGENCY NAME] will keep records, set goals and standards, and implement changes based on the data (.14C). Every death is reviewed through the QA committee.

definitions.definition: The written quality assurance plan approved by DDA, describing goals, measures, data sources, responsible persons and review frequency.
Any change to the QA plan that alters its goals, measures, methods or responsibilities, as opposed to a clerical correction.
A record of each use of a restrictive technique under a behavior plan: individual, medication or technique, date and time, whether emergency or planned, and effectiveness.
A structured review of the circumstances of an individual's death, conducted through the QA committee to identify lessons and system improvements.
The DDA Policy on Reportable Incidents and Investigations. [AGENCY NAME] follows it for incident reporting and review.

procedures: The governing body appoints a QA designee, who reports to the Program Director, to coordinate the QA plan and data collection.

[ADMINISTRATOR NAME] and the QA designee draft the QA plan with measurable goals and standards covering, at minimum, individual satisfaction and choice, health and safety, incidents, rights restrictions, behavior supports, staffing and training, medication errors, and Medicaid documentation (see GOV-06).

The plan is submitted to DDA with the license application, and any substantive change is submitted to DDA for approval before it takes effect (.14A). The submission and DDA's approval are kept in the QA file. The QA plan is not treated as final until DDA approves it.

The QA designee or another qualified staff member makes personal contact with each individual at least quarterly. This is a face-to-face or other direct conversation, using communication supports the person needs, to ask about satisfaction, choices and preferences. The responses are recorded in the QA file.

The QA designee collects data monthly from incident reports, medication error reports, grievances, rights restriction logs, restrictive technique logs, health events, staffing and training records and contact results.

The restrictive technique log records, for each use under a behavior plan, the individual, the medication or technique, the date and time, whether the use was an emergency or planned, and its effectiveness (.14B(4)). The designee reviews the log monthly and sends it to the standing committee (see BH-03).

The QA designee analyzes the data quarterly for trends by individual, site, staff, time of day and type of event, and prepares a written report for the Program Director, standing committee and governing body.

If data or a single event shows that health or safety is at risk, the Program Director acts promptly, within 24 hours or sooner as the risk requires. The action taken and the date are documented and reported to [ADMINISTRATOR NAME].
The governing body reviews the quarterly report, approves corrective actions with responsible persons and due dates, and records them in the minutes. The QA designee tracks them to completion.

The QA plan goals and standards are reviewed at least annually to determine whether they are being met. Changes are implemented from the data (.14C), and any substantive change goes to DDA under step 3.
[AGENCY NAME] keeps records sufficient to show DDA that its goals are being met, and produces them promptly on request.
When an individual dies, the Program Director notifies [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] immediately and reports the death under DDA incident requirements (see HW-05 and BH-05).

Within a time frame set by the standing committee, the QA committee conducts a mortality review of every death. The review covers the circumstances, health history, supports provided, any incident or investigation findings, and whether care or systems should change. The committee also reviews any additional information or process DDA requires, and [AGENCY NAME] will follow the DDA mortality review requirements in effect at the time.

The committee records its conclusions and recommendations in confidential minutes. The Program Director implements approved recommendations and the QA designee follows them to completion. Confidential information is protected under Health-General §7-1010.
The governing body receives an annual QA summary, including trend data, mortality review themes, corrective actions and their results.

responsibilities.duty: Approves the QA plan, reviews reports and ensures corrective actions are completed.
Submits the QA plan and substantive changes to DDA and ensures resources for QA activities.
Collects and analyzes data, makes personal contact with individuals, prepares reports and tracks corrective actions.
Responds promptly to health and safety risks and implements changes.
Reviews incident and restrictive technique data and conducts mortality reviews.

documentation: DDA-approved QA plan and approval correspondence
Individual contact and satisfaction records
Monthly data summaries and quarterly trend reports
Restrictive technique tracking log
Records of prompt responses to health or safety risks
Governing body and committee minutes with corrective action tracking
Mortality review records (confidential)

policies.title: Standing Committee (Human Rights / Quality Assurance / Incident Review)
policies.applies_to: Standing committee members, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], Program Director, QA designee, behavior support staff
policies.purpose: To establish the standing committee required by COMAR 10.22.02.14E, which protects individuals' rights, reviews incidents, approves restrictive behavior plans and supports quality assurance.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a standing committee that performs quality assurance functions, reviews the incident protocol and all incidents, approves all behavior plans that use restrictive techniques, reviews and sets time frames for rights restrictions not related to challenging behavior, and reviews policies for the protection of rights (.14E(1)). Membership has equal numbers of licensee staff and non-employees. No member decides on incidents or behavior plans they were involved in. The committee protects confidentiality under Health-General §7-1010.

definitions.definition: The committee under COMAR 10.22.02.14E that carries out human rights, quality assurance and incident review functions.

A member who is an individual receiving services, a proponent or a community member and is not an employee of [AGENCY NAME]. A member paid only for committee service counts as neither staff nor non-employee for balance purposes (.14E(3)).
A technique in a behavior plan that restricts an individual's movement, access or rights, which requires committee approval before use.

definitions.term: Rights restriction not related to challenging behavior
definitions.definition: A limit on a fundamental right that is imposed for reasons other than challenging behavior and must have time frames set by the committee.

procedures: The governing body appoints committee members and records the appointments in its minutes. The committee has equal numbers of [AGENCY NAME] staff members and non-employees, who are individuals, proponents or community members (.14E(3)).

[ADMINISTRATOR NAME] keeps a committee roster that shows each member's category (staff or non-employee). The roster is rechecked before every meeting, and a member paid only for committee service is counted as neither staff nor non-employee.

The committee meets as needed, and at least quarterly, with a majority of members present (.14E(6)). A meeting where a majority is not present does not make decisions. The chair sets the agenda and the secretary records minutes.

At the start of each meeting, members declare any involvement in the matters on the agenda. A member who was involved in an incident or who developed a behavior plan takes no part in the decision on that incident or plan (.14E(5)), and the minutes record the recusal.

The committee reviews the incident protocol at least annually. It reviews all incidents, including trends, investigation results and corrective actions, at each meeting. The Program Director supplies incident summaries in advance (see BH-05).

No behavior plan that uses a restrictive technique may be implemented until the committee has approved it. The behavior support professional presents the plan, data and less restrictive alternatives tried. The committee's decision, conditions and review date are recorded (see BH-01 and BH-02).

The committee reviews each rights restriction that is not related to challenging behavior and sets a time frame for it, after which it must be reviewed again. The Program Director ensures the restriction is not continued past that time frame without a new committee review (see IR-02).
The committee reviews the restrictive technique tracking data and the use of medications to modify behavior at least quarterly (see BH-03).
The committee reviews policies, and their implementation, for protection of legal and human rights, and gives recommendations to the governing body (see GOV-03).

The committee may consult a psychologist, physician, physician assistant, nurse practitioner or board-certified clinical pharmacist when a matter requires clinical expertise (.14E(4)). The consultant's name, credentials and advice are recorded in the minutes.
Members receive training on the committee's role, individual rights and confidentiality before first participating, and a signed confidentiality agreement is kept on file.

Minutes record attendance, the number present, recusals, matters reviewed, decisions, time frames and responsible persons. Minutes are stored in a locked or access-restricted location and shared only as needed, in line with Health-General §7-1010 (.14E(7)) (see IR-04).
The Program Director tracks every committee action item to completion and reports status at the next meeting. Overdue items are escalated to [ADMINISTRATOR NAME].
The committee chair reports to the governing body after each meeting and annually summarizes the committee's work.

responsibilities.duty: Convenes meetings, ensures a majority is present, manages recusals and reports to the governing body.
Review incidents, behavior plans, rights restrictions and policies, and protect confidentiality.
Maintains the roster and ensures the committee is balanced and resourced.
Provides incident, restriction and behavior plan information and carries out committee decisions.
Records and safeguards the minutes.

documentation: Committee roster showing member categories
Governing body appointment records
Meeting agendas, sign-in sheets and minutes, including recusals
Approvals of behavior plans with restrictive techniques
Rights restriction reviews with time frames
Incident review records and action item tracking
Consultant advice records
Signed member confidentiality agreements

policies.title: Medicaid Compliance, Billing, Retainer Days and Service Documentation
policies.applies_to: Governing body, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], Program Director, billing staff, residential staff who document services
policies.purpose: To ensure [AGENCY NAME] bills Medicaid only for authorized Community Living – Group Home services that were actually delivered and documented, and that residential claims are submitted accurately.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] bills W5600 Community Living – Group Home per person per day through LTSSMaryland, only for services in the individual's approved Person-Centered Plan (PCP) and Detailed Service Authorization (Appendix I). Room and board are never billed to Medicaid and are collected from the resident under a written agreement. The 'Number of People Authorized' on each claim is entered accurately, because it determines the daily rate. Retainer days are limited to 18 per person per year. No payment is made under the waiver to relatives, legal guardians or legally responsible persons for this service. Daily documentation supports every billed day.

definitions.definition: The LTSSMaryland billing code for Community Living – Group Home, billed per person per day.
The number of people living in the home and present, or on retainer days, which determines the residential daily rate.
A day for which the residence is held for a person who is temporarily away (hospitalization, behavioral respite or visits with family or friends), up to 18 per person per year.
The authorization in LTSSMaryland that specifies the services, units and period that may be billed.
The billing code for dedicated 1:1 hours, billed per 15-minute unit.
Electronic Visit Verification. It is required for Personal Supports and Respite but not for Community Living – Group Home.

procedures: The billing office confirms that the site's own DDA Licensed Site MA number is active in MPRIME before any claim for that site is submitted (see GOV-02).

Before billing starts for a person, the Program Director confirms that the approved PCP and the Detailed Service Authorization in LTSSMaryland include Community Living – Group Home and any dedicated hours. The billing office files a copy. Services not on the authorization are never billed.

The billing office bills W5600 per person per day, based on the daily attendance record. A day is billable only when the person was in residence or on a properly documented retainer day, and the daily documentation supports it (see PC-03).

For each claim, the billing office enters the 'Number of People Authorized' using the daily census (people living in the home and present, plus people on retainer days). The census is reviewed by the Program Director before each billing cycle.

When a resident moves out or is discharged, the Program Director notifies the billing office the same day. The billing office adjusts claims from the effective date, understanding that the rate for the remaining residents changes (for example, from $403.30 to $355.23 per day when a 4-person home drops to 3 residents at the October 1, 2026 standard rate). [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] reviews the financial effect of any vacancy and plans for it.

Retainer days are used only for hospitalization, behavioral respite, or family or friend visits. The billing office keeps a running count per person per calendar year, and the Program Director gets written notice when a person reaches 14 days. No retainer day beyond 18 per person per year is billed.

Dedicated 1:1 hours (W1999) are billed only as authorized. They may be shared among participants only in the situations the waiver permits (a retired person, a person transitioning to retirement, a person recovering from an illness or injury, or a person with few day-service hours). The threshold in the current waiver text is under 40 hours, and under 30 hours in pending Amendment #4. The Program Director confirms which threshold applies. The sharing is documented in each affected person's PCP and bills for one participant only.
Room and board are excluded from the Medicaid rate. The billing office collects room and board from the resident under the residency agreement and never includes them in a Medicaid claim (see IR-08).

No relative, legal guardian or legally responsible person is paid with waiver funds for Community Living – Group Home services. [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] verifies this in the hiring file for any worker with a family relationship to an individual (see ST-06).
The billing office does not submit EVV records for Community Living – Group Home. It uses EVV only if [AGENCY NAME] is separately authorized to deliver services for which EVV is required.

Before each claim submission, the billing office compares claims to attendance records, daily service documentation and the authorization, and records the reviewer's initials. Discrepancies are resolved before submission.
The Program Director reviews daily documentation for completeness at least weekly. Missing or late notes are corrected and the delinquent staff retrained (see PC-03).

The billing office warns [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] that payment may not be received for up to 180 days from the start of service, and the budget plans for this delay before any new site admits individuals.

The billing office monitors the pending 2% FY2027 rate reduction. Until CMS approves the waiver amendment, rates remain at June 30, 2026 levels. [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] reports any rate change to the board and the billing office applies a new rate only after receiving official notice.

[AGENCY NAME] performs a documented internal billing audit at least quarterly on a sample of claims, comparing each claim to the authorization and documentation. Overpayments are reported and repaid promptly under direction from [ADMINISTRATOR NAME]. Findings go to the governing body and the QA plan (see GOV-04).
The compliance designee screens staff and contractors for exclusion from federal and state programs (see GOV-02). No claim is submitted for services delivered by an excluded person.
Billing records, authorizations, attendance records and supporting documentation are kept at least 6 years and are available for review by DDA, OHCQ, Maryland Medicaid and other authorized reviewers.

responsibilities.duty: Oversees Medicaid compliance and reviews billing audit results.
Ensures billing practices follow waiver rules and responds to rate changes, audits and repayment obligations.
Submits accurate W5600 and any W1999 claims, tracks retainer days, reconciles census and performs internal audits.
Verifies census and daily documentation, and notifies the billing office of moves, hospital stays and absences the same day.
Complete daily documentation accurately and on time.

documentation: Approved PCP and Detailed Service Authorization for each individual
Daily census and attendance records
Daily service documentation
Retainer day log with annual counts per person
Claim submissions and remittances
Dedicated hours sharing documentation in the PCP
Pre-billing reconciliation records and quarterly billing audit reports
Room and board collection records, kept separate from Medicaid billing
Records of any overpayment, correction or repayment

policies.title: Program Service Plan Maintenance and DDA Approval of Changes
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Administrator, Program Director, QA staff and all sites operated under the Community Living – Group Home service
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] operates exactly as described in its DDA-approved Program Service Plan (PSP), keeps the PSP current, and never changes the service model before DDA approves the change.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a PSP for each service it provides, including Community Living – Group Home. The PSP describes the rationale, scope, staffing and training, and the setting and location of the service, including the number of individuals expected to be served in each home. The agency follows every provision of the approved PSP. A revised PSP is submitted to DDA and approved before any change is implemented. The Administrator ensures the governing body reviews and updates the PSP at least every 3 years. An alternative service model is not used unless DDA approves it through an innovative PSP variance. The PSP must stay within the scope of community residential services defined for group homes.

definitions.definition: The written plan, approved by DDA, that describes the rationale, scope, staffing and training, and setting and location of a licensed service.
Any change to the PSP's rationale, scope, staffing pattern, required training, setting or location, or the number of individuals expected to be served in a home.
A DDA approval that allows an alternative service model that does not fit the standard PSP requirements.
The [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] or other person with day-to-day authority over the licensee's operations.

procedures: The Administrator keeps the current DDA-approved PSP for Community Living – Group Home in the Governance File at [ADDRESS] and in the secure electronic policy folder. Only the approved version is in use.

The Administrator confirms that the PSP covers rationale, scope, staffing and training, and setting and location, including the expected number of individuals per home. Any missing element is corrected through a revision submitted to DDA.

The Administrator records the date of DDA's last PSP approval and sets the next governing body review date no more than 3 years later. This date is entered on the Compliance Calendar, with a reminder 90 days before it is due.
At least 90 days before the review date, the Administrator prepares a PSP review packet. It includes the current PSP, the QA data summary, staffing and training records, and any proposed changes.
The governing body reviews the packet at a scheduled meeting, votes to affirm or update the PSP, and records the decision in the minutes.

Before any operational change, the Program Director completes a PSP Change Screening Form. It asks whether the change affects rationale, scope, staffing or training, setting or location, or the number of individuals served.
If the answer to any question is yes, the change is a substantive change. The Administrator drafts a revised PSP and presents it to the governing body for approval before submission.
The Administrator submits the revised PSP to DDA as DDA directs and keeps proof of submission. No one implements the change until DDA's written approval is received.
The Administrator files the approval letter with the PSP. The Administrator then updates the staffing plan, training plan, residency agreements and site records to match, and logs the effective date.
If DDA asks for more information or denies the revision, the Administrator responds in the time DDA gives. The agency continues to operate under the previously approved PSP.

If the agency wants an alternative model, the Administrator first obtains governing body approval to request an innovative PSP variance. The agency does not start that model until DDA approves it in writing.
Within 14 days of any DDA approval, the Program Director gives staff a summary of the approved changes and has each staff member sign the training acknowledgment.

At each home, the Program Director compares actual staffing, training and the number of residents with the PSP every quarter. Gaps are reported to the Administrator within 5 business days and corrected, or a PSP revision is started.
The QA Coordinator includes PSP compliance (the quarterly comparison and the 3-year review status) in the annual QA report to the governing body (see GOV-04).
The Administrator keeps all PSP versions, DDA correspondence, governing body minutes and Change Screening Forms for the life of the license plus the retention period in RC-01.

responsibilities.duty: Reviews and updates the PSP at least every 3 years and approves each proposed revision before submission.
Ensures the 3-year review occurs, submits revisions to DDA, and prevents implementation before DDA approval.
Completes Change Screening Forms, performs quarterly PSP comparisons and trains staff on approved changes.
Reports PSP compliance and review status in the annual QA report.

documentation: Current and prior DDA-approved PSPs
PSP Change Screening Forms
Proof of submission and DDA approval letters
Governing body minutes recording PSP reviews and approvals
Quarterly PSP comparison reports
Staff training acknowledgments for PSP changes

policies.title: Licensed Capacity, New Site, Relocation and Closure
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Administrator, Program Director, Residential Coordinator and all sites
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] never serves more people than its license allows, and that every new site, relocation or closure is approved by DDA in advance and protects the individuals who live there.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] serves no more individuals at a site than the number stated on its license. The agency does not exceed licensed capacity without prior approval from the DDA Director, which is limited to 60 days plus one 60-day extension. No home exceeds 4 residents unless DDA previously approved a different number, and each resident has a private bedroom. The agency obtains DDA approval at least 30 days before opening, closing or relocating any site. It lists each site, its capacity and its proposed occupancy date on DDA Addendum DD.ADD.1.0, including the Community Settings Rule attestation. It does not admit anyone to a new site until DDA approves it and OHCQ completes the required survey. Voluntary surrender of the license, and any termination of services to an individual, follow the notice and approval requirements below.

definitions.definition: The number of individuals the license states may be served at a site.

definitions.term: DDA Addendum for Licensed Services and Sites (DD.ADD.1.0)
definitions.definition: The DDA form that lists each site, capacity requested and proposed occupancy date. It includes the Community Settings Rule attestation and a question on wheelchair accessibility.
The DDA inspection form for new sites. It covers institutional or isolating characteristics, heightened scrutiny (including proximity to the provider's other sites) and settings-rule items.
The licensee's request to give up its license and stop operating, which requires a closure schedule approved by the DDA Director.

procedures: Before any site, bedroom or admission decision, the Program Director checks the licensed capacity on the posted license and the DDA-approved site record. The Residential Coordinator keeps a current census for each home.
No admission is made if it would exceed the licensed capacity. The Administrator is notified the same day of any proposed admission that would bring a home to its limit.

If an emergency makes it necessary to exceed capacity, only the Administrator may request DDA Director approval, in writing and before the additional person is served. The request states the reason, the number of days requested (up to 60) and the safety plan. If an extension (one 60-day maximum) is needed, the Administrator requests it before the first period ends.
The Administrator records the approval dates and end date in the Capacity Log and tells the governing body at its next meeting.

To open a site, the governing body approves the site proposal. The Administrator confirms it will have no more than 4 residents (or has prior DDA approval for a different number) and private bedrooms for all residents.

The Administrator screens the proposed site against the DDA New Site Visit Checklist before signing a lease or purchase. The screen covers institutional or isolating characteristics, location in the community, and proximity to the agency's other sites. A site that fails or raises heightened-scrutiny concerns is not pursued without DDA guidance.

The Administrator completes DDA Addendum DD.ADD.1.0 for the site. It lists the site address, requested capacity, proposed occupancy date and wheelchair accessibility, and includes the Community Settings Rule attestation. The Administrator signs the attestation only after verifying each condition on site.

The Administrator submits the request to DDA so that approval is received at least 30 days before the proposed opening, closing or relocation. The Administrator keeps proof of submission and the approval letter.

After DDA approval, the agency prepares for the OHCQ survey of the site. The Program Director completes a readiness walk-through using the New Site Visit Checklist, and the Administrator corrects deficiencies before the survey. No individual moves in until the site is cleared to open.

For a relocation, the Program Director meets with each affected individual, proponent, and team in person at least 30 days before the move, or sooner if possible. Each person's preferences about housing, roommates and location are recorded and respected, and the move is documented in the individual's plan (see PC-02).
For a site closure, the agency does not move any individual until DDA approves the closure and the individual's team has agreed to the new placement. Transition steps follow PC-05.

To voluntarily surrender the license, the governing body votes to approve it. The Administrator submits a closure schedule to the DDA Director at least 90 days before the planned closure date. The agency keeps operating under the schedule, and if the Director requires up to 90 more days of operation, the agency continues services without interruption.

The agency does not terminate services to an individual except for good cause with the DDA Director's written approval. The Administrator gives the Director 90 days' written notice. The individual and proponent receive written notice of the right to a hearing under COMAR 10.22.16, and copies go to the regional office and the individual's team. Services are considered terminated after 60 consecutive days of absence unless the Director decides otherwise, so the Program Director reports any extended absence to the Administrator at 30 days.

The Administrator reviews billing impact before any admission, discharge or vacancy decision. The billing rate depends on the number of people living in the home, and a vacancy lowers the daily rate for the other residents. Financial considerations never override an individual's choice, safety or rights.
The Administrator updates the PSP when the number of individuals expected in a home changes (see GOV-07) and updates licensing and Medicaid records for each site (see GOV-02).

responsibilities.duty: Approves new sites, relocations, closures and any request to surrender the license.
Submits all DDA requests and addenda on time, controls capacity exceptions and signs the Community Settings Rule attestation.
Maintains the census, prevents over-capacity admissions, runs site readiness walk-throughs and leads individual and proponent communication during moves.
Keeps the current census and bedroom assignments and monitors extended absences.

documentation: Posted license and site capacity record
Capacity Log with any Director approvals
Completed DDA Addendum DD.ADD.1.0 and DDA approval letters
New Site Visit Checklist self-review
Governing body minutes approving site actions
Closure schedule and DDA correspondence
Individual and proponent notices and transition records

policies.title: Regulatory Surveys, Complaint Investigations and Plans of Correction
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Administrator, Program Director, all staff and all sites
policies.purpose: To prepare [AGENCY NAME] for OHCQ surveys and investigations, to give surveyors full cooperation, and to submit acceptable plans of correction on time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] cooperates fully with the Maryland Department of Health Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ), which acts as DDA's agent to monitor and inspect licensees. The agency expects an on-site pre-licensure survey, announced and unannounced licensure visits at least annually, and announced or unannounced complaint investigation visits. The agency submits a plan of correction (POC) at the exit conference or within 10 working days of receiving the findings. It submits sooner if OHCQ requires, and if a POC is rejected, it submits a revised POC within 10 working days. The agency treats immediate jeopardy (Priority 1) matters as emergencies, since OHCQ begins those investigations within 2 working days.

definitions.definition: The Maryland Department of Health Office of Health Care Quality, the licensing and monitoring agent for DDA. Its Developmental Disabilities Team can be reached at 410-402-8100 or 877-402-8220.
The agency's written response to survey findings, stating how and when each deficiency will be corrected and how the agency will keep it corrected.
A situation that has caused or is likely to cause serious harm to an individual. OHCQ investigates these within 2 working days.
Monday through Friday, excluding State holidays.

procedures: The Administrator posts the OHCQ Developmental Disabilities contact numbers (410-402-8100 / 877-402-8220) in the office and at each home, and gives them to every supervisor.

The Program Director keeps a Survey Readiness Binder at each home, with the license, current PSP, emergency plan, drill records, staff schedule, training records, individual records, and QA records, so that surveyors can be given access at any time of day.

Any staff member on duty who is told that surveyors have arrived asks for identification, lets them in, and calls the Program Director and Administrator immediately. Staff do not refuse entry, delay a survey or coach individuals on what to say.
The Program Director or designee accompanies surveyors, provides requested records promptly, keeps a list of everything copied or removed, and protects confidentiality of records not requested.
Individuals have the right to speak with surveyors privately. Staff support them to do so if they wish, and no staff member retaliates in any way.

At the exit conference, the Administrator or designee takes notes, asks for clarification of findings and records the date and time findings were received. Any immediate safety hazard is corrected before surveyors leave, where possible.
If surveyors identify immediate jeopardy, the Administrator takes immediate action to protect individuals, notifies the governing body chair the same day, and documents the corrective action taken.

The Administrator logs the date the written findings are received and calendars the POC due date, which is 10 working days from receipt, or earlier if OHCQ requires. If the agency cannot meet the deadline, the Administrator requests an extension from the OHCQ Director in writing before the deadline. Extensions can be up to 30 days.

For each deficiency, the Administrator assigns a responsible person and writes the POC. It includes the immediate correction, steps to find others who might be affected, systemic changes, a completion date and the person responsible for monitoring.

The Administrator presents the POC to the governing body for approval, as the agency's bylaws require, and the governing body records its decision in the minutes. If the POC is due before the next meeting, the Administrator arranges a special or electronic review.
The Administrator submits the POC to OHCQ at the exit conference or within the deadline and keeps proof of submission.
If OHCQ rejects the POC, the Administrator revises it and resubmits within 10 working days of receiving the rejection. The governing body is informed of the revision.

The Program Director completes each correction by the date in the POC, saves the evidence (such as training sign-in sheets, updated policies, and photos), and reports progress to the Administrator weekly until all items are closed.

The QA Coordinator tracks every cited deficiency in the QA system, audits corrected items at 30, 60 and 90 days after completion, and reports results to the governing body and standing committee (see GOV-04 and GOV-05).

For a complaint investigation, the Administrator identifies who may be interviewed, preserves all relevant records, does not alter or backdate any record, and ensures staff and individuals are free from retaliation.
The Administrator keeps all survey reports, POCs, OHCQ correspondence and evidence of correction in the Regulatory File for the retention period in RC-01.

responsibilities.duty: Approves POC responses and monitors correction of deficiencies.
Leads survey response, meets POC deadlines, requests extensions where needed and corresponds with OHCQ.
Maintains survey readiness at each home, accompanies surveyors and implements corrections.
Tracks deficiencies and audits sustained compliance.
Cooperate with surveyors, notify supervisors immediately and never retaliate against anyone who speaks with surveyors.

documentation: Survey Readiness Binder checklist
Survey sign-in and record-copy logs
OHCQ statements of deficiencies and exit-conference notes
Plans of correction, revised POCs and proof of submission
Extension requests and OHCQ responses
Governing body minutes approving POCs
Evidence of correction and follow-up audits

policies.title: Conflict of Interest and Fiscal Management
policies.applies_to: Governing body members, administrators, employees, care providers, volunteers, consultants and standing committee members
policies.purpose: To make sure decisions at [AGENCY NAME] are made in the interest of the individuals served and the agency, free from personal financial gain, and that funds are managed according to sound accounting practice.
policies.policy: No governing body member, employee, care provider, volunteer or standing committee member may have a financial or personal conflict of interest in the agency's operations. Fiscal affairs are managed under generally accepted accounting practices. Governing body members and employees may not own property that is leased back to [AGENCY NAME]. Relatives, legal guardians and legally responsible persons of an individual may not be paid to provide Community Living – Group Home services to that individual. Individuals' funds are kept separate from agency funds.

definitions.definition: A situation in which a person's financial, family or other personal interest could influence, or appear to influence, their duties to the agency or the individuals served.
A person or business connected to a board member, employee or their immediate family by ownership, employment, family or financial interest.
A person with a legal duty to support an individual, such as a spouse or, for a minor, a parent.
The standard accounting rules and conventions used to record, report and audit an organization's finances.

procedures: Before taking office or starting work, every governing body member, employee, care provider, volunteer, consultant and standing committee member completes and signs a Conflict of Interest Disclosure Form. The Administrator holds the forms in the Governance File.
Each person updates the disclosure annually, and within 10 days of any change in circumstances.
The Administrator reviews all disclosures within 30 days of receipt and presents any potential conflict to the governing body chair (or the full board if the Administrator is involved).

A person with a conflict discloses it at the start of any meeting where the matter is discussed, leaves the room, does not vote and does not try to influence the decision. Minutes record the disclosure and recusal.

Any contract or purchase with a related party needs governing body approval by disinterested members after reviewing at least two competing quotes. The governing body records why the arrangement is in the agency's best interest.

The agency does not lease, rent or buy any home, vehicle or other property from a governing body member or employee, or from their immediate family members, if the property is leased back to the agency. The Administrator checks the ownership of every lease before signing, and the agency does not enter the lease if the owner is a board member or employee.
Governing body members who are voting members are not employees or immediate family of employees. The Administrator checks this at board appointment and annually.

The agency does not hire or pay a relative, legal guardian or legally responsible person to provide Community Living – Group Home services to that individual. Hiring is blocked at the application stage, and payroll reviews this each quarter. Any exception request is referred to the Administrator and DDA.

Staff may not accept gifts of more than nominal value, loans, or inheritance from individuals or proponents, and may not borrow from or lend to them (see ST-07). Staff report any offer to the Program Director the same day.

The governing body approves an annual budget before the fiscal year begins. The Administrator provides monthly financial statements prepared under GAAP to the governing body, including revenue, expenses, cash position and accounts receivable.

The agency uses a chart of accounts, separate bank accounts for operating funds, and written procedures that separate the duties of authorizing, recording and reconciling transactions. Two signatures or approvals are required over [DOLLAR AMOUNT] set by the governing body.
