Meals for residents with modified textures or choking risk are prepared exactly as ordered. Staff use the correct equipment, give appropriate supervision and positioning, and follow the resident's choking risk plan under HW-03. Staff stop the meal and call for help if the resident coughs, chokes or shows signs of distress, and follow emergency steps in HW-04.

The Home Manager keeps food safely: refrigerated foods are kept at or below 41°F and frozen foods at 0°F, leftovers are labeled and dated, perishable food is not left out, and counters, cutting boards and utensils are cleaned and sanitized after use. Staff follow hand washing under HE-03.
Staff and residents who prepare food follow safe handling practices. Residents who want to cook are supported in doing so, with training and adaptations in the IP, and with safety supports as needed.

Staff record meal intake, weights, fluid intake or other monitoring only when the IP or physician orders it, and report significant changes (weight loss or gain, refusal to eat, swallowing difficulties, dehydration signs) to the Home Manager and Delegating Nurse the same day. The nurse follows up with the health care provider under HW-02 and HW-03.

When a resident goes on an outing, to day activities, or travels, staff bring or arrange food that follows the diet order and allergy information, and brief the other people who will be responsible, in accordance with HE-05.

Staff do not use food as a reward or punishment, and do not withhold food, or alter a diet, as a consequence for behavior. Any such action is treated as a rights violation under IR-01 and IR-02 and reported under BH-04.
Residents may keep their own food in the home, and may have meals out and take part in community dining, as chosen. Staff support access to transportation for grocery shopping and dining out.

The Delegating Nurse reviews every modified diet at least annually, and on any change of condition, hospitalization or provider change, and updates instructions. The Program Director confirms IP updates are completed.

The Home Manager audits each home monthly for stocked food, kitchen safety, diet compliance and posted allergy information, and records the findings. The Program Director addresses deficiencies promptly and reports trends under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures IPs include allergies, diets and any food modifications and that rights modifications are reviewed through the proper process.
Reviews diet orders, writes staff instructions, trains staff, monitors nutrition and swallowing concerns, and coordinates with providers.
Keeps food stocked and safe, posts allergy information, supervises staff on meal-time safety, and audits compliance.
Support resident food choices, follow diet orders exactly, report concerns, and never withhold food or use it as a consequence.
Make food choices, share preferences and health information, and take part in decisions about modifications.

documentation: Recorded allergies and diagnoses in the individual record
Physician diet orders and IP diet entries
Staff training records on modified diets
Menu planning records and resident preference records
IP documentation and consent for any modification of access to food
Monitoring records ordered by a provider (weights, intake)
Monthly home audit records on food and kitchen safety

policies.title: Transportation and Vehicle Safety
policies.applies_to: All staff, volunteers and contractors who drive or arrange transportation for residents, and all vehicles used to transport residents
policies.purpose: To make sure residents can get to the places they choose and need to go, safely and reliably, using the most cost-effective mode and with proper insurance and driver qualifications.
policies.policy: Transportation is included in the Community Living – Group Home daily rate, and [AGENCY NAME] will provide or arrange it for residents without charging them separately. [AGENCY NAME] will use the most cost-effective mode of transportation that meets the resident's needs and preferences. Staff who drive will hold a valid driver's license, and all vehicles used to transport residents will be insured. Auto insurance documentation will be maintained as required in the DDA application (Attachment 12). Emergency information and medication plans will go with residents on outings, and residents will be transported only as the Individual Plan (IP) provides.

definitions.definition: The least costly means of transportation that safely and reasonably meets the resident's need and choice, such as walking, public transit, paratransit, rides with family or friends, or an agency vehicle.
A vehicle owned, leased or controlled by [AGENCY NAME] and used to transport residents.
Any trip away from the home with a resident, whether for appointments, work, recreation, shopping, religious services or community events.

procedures: The Program Director confirms that transportation costs are covered by the daily rate and that no resident is charged for transportation to services, medical care or community activities that the IP requires. Residents' personal spending (for example, personal outings paid with their own funds) is handled under IR-05.

During person-centered planning, the team identifies each resident's transportation needs and preferences, including work, medical visits, day activities, religious services, visits with family and friends, and recreation. The IP records the mode, level of staff support, supervision, and any adaptive equipment.

The Home Manager chooses the most cost-effective mode that meets each need, such as public transit, paratransit, rides from family, or an agency vehicle, and documents the choice. Residents are supported and trained in using public transportation where they are able and wish to, in line with community integration under PC-04.

Before a staff member is allowed to drive residents, the Home Manager checks a copy of the staff member's valid driver's license, records the expiration date, and obtains a current driving record review as [AGENCY NAME]'s insurer requires. Staff who lose or have their license suspended notify the Home Manager before the next shift and are immediately removed from driving.

The Program Director confirms that every vehicle used to transport residents, including a staff member's personal vehicle if used for business, is registered and insured, and keeps the current insurance documentation, including the auto insurance documentation required in DDA application Attachment 12. Insurance renewals are tracked on a calendar.

Staff driving agency vehicles perform a pre-trip check of tires, lights, brakes, fluids and seat belts, and report defects. The Home Manager schedules preventive maintenance, records repairs, and removes any unsafe vehicle from service.

Each agency vehicle carries a first aid kit, flashlight, emergency contact list, vehicle registration and insurance card, and a fire extinguisher or other emergency equipment if the vehicle type requires it. The Home Manager checks the kit monthly.

All occupants use seat belts or approved restraint systems. Residents who use wheelchairs are transported in a vehicle with a working lift or ramp, and their wheelchairs are secured by the four-point tie-down system and with a lap and shoulder belt used according to the manufacturer's instructions. Only trained staff operate lifts and securement equipment.

Staff driving residents do not use handheld phones, text, or drive while impaired or drowsy. Staff follow all traffic laws. A staff member who has a motor vehicle accident or traffic citation while on duty reports it to the Program Director immediately.

Before each outing, the staff member brings an emergency information sheet for each resident, with name, diagnoses, allergies, medications, physician, emergency contacts and guardian or proponent information. Staff also bring a copy of the resident's emergency medical information so that emergency personnel can use it.

For outings that cover scheduled medication times, staff bring medication in labeled containers and administer it according to HW-01, or only staff who are certified to do so give it. Medication taken on outings is packaged separately and recorded on the Medication Administration Record. Staff bring diet-appropriate food and fluids under HE-04.

Staff transport only the residents whose IP provides for that trip, and supervise at the level the IP requires. Staffing for outings is planned so that residents remaining at home still have required supervision under ST-01.

Staff do not transport residents in a personal vehicle unless the Program Director has given advance approval, the vehicle is insured for that purpose, and the resident has agreed. Staff never leave a resident unattended in a vehicle.

If a vehicle breaks down or an accident happens, staff move residents to safety, call 911 if anyone is hurt, notify the Home Manager and Program Director, arrange replacement transportation, and complete an incident report under BH-05 when required. Any resident injury is evaluated under HW-04.
If a resident leaves the group or cannot be located during an outing, staff follow BH-06 immediately.

The Program Director reviews license and insurance compliance, vehicle maintenance, and transportation incidents every quarter, and reports results under GOV-04. Transportation is also reviewed for access to community activities and work.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains insurance, including the auto insurance documentation for the DDA application; approves drivers and vehicles; reviews incidents and compliance.
Verifies driver's licenses; schedules vehicle maintenance; plans transportation and staffing for outings; checks emergency kits.
Drive and transport safely, secure residents, bring emergency information and medication, and report accidents and vehicle problems.
State transportation preferences and take part in planning how they travel.

documentation: Valid driver's license copies and driving record reviews for each driver
Auto insurance documentation for all vehicles, including DDA application Attachment 12
Vehicle registration, maintenance and repair logs, and pre-trip checklists
IP transportation section, with modes, supports and supervision levels
Emergency information sheets and outing medication records
Accident and incident reports
Quarterly transportation compliance review

policies.title: Staffing Plan, Supervision and Overnight Coverage
policies.applies_to: Program Director, Home Managers, scheduling personnel and all direct support staff at [AGENCY NAME]'s licensed sites
policies.purpose: To make sure each home is staffed so that every resident's health and safety needs are met and the services in the Individual Plan (IP) are delivered, 24 hours a day.
policies.policy: Maryland sets no fixed staff ratio. [AGENCY NAME] will analyze the number of individuals served and each person's needs, and will develop and implement a written staffing plan for each home that meets health and safety needs and delivers the services in the IP (COMAR 10.22.02.11A). Staffing levels and patterns will follow the IP (COMAR 10.22.08.04A). Services will be available 24 hours a day, seven days a week at every licensed site, with back-up and emergency support. Overnight coverage, awake or asleep, will be set by each person's assessed needs and the IP. DDA's rate assumption of 43.14 staff-hours per day for a four-person home with overnight supervision is used only as a planning benchmark and is not a regulatory ratio. Any person who meets the training requirements and has no disqualifying criminal history may be included in the staffing plan.

definitions.definition: A written plan for each home stating the number of staff by shift, the roles and qualifications needed, overnight coverage, back-up and emergency support, and how the plan was derived from residents' needs and IPs.
A staff member who is awake and alert and on duty throughout the overnight period.
A staff member who is on site and available during the overnight period and can respond promptly, where the IP and assessed needs permit this level of coverage.
On-call arrangements that assure a qualified person can reach the home promptly when a scheduled staff member is absent or an emergency requires more help.
A figure used for budget and scheduling purposes (for example, 43.14 staff-hours per day) that does not replace the individualized analysis of residents' needs.

procedures: Before a home opens, and then at least annually, the Program Director and Home Manager analyze the number of residents and each person's assessed needs, including medical, behavioral, mobility, communication, supervision, community, and employment support needs, using each IP, assessments, risk plans (for example seizure, choking, and behavior plans), and nursing input.

The Program Director writes a staffing plan for each home. For every shift and day of the week it states the number of staff, any specific skills or certifications required (for example Medication Technician certification, behavior plan training, or lift operation), any one-to-one or shared support hours, and the way community and employment activities are covered.

The plan identifies overnight coverage, awake or asleep, based on each resident's assessed needs and IP, including medical risks, seizures, behaviors, mobility, and ability to call for help or evacuate. The reasoning is recorded. COMAR 10.22.02.11 does not require awake overnight staff, so any change in overnight coverage is made only after the IP team reviews it and the IP is updated.

The Program Director compares the staffing plan with the DDA rate benchmark of 43.14 staff-hours per day for a four-person home with overnight supervision, as a planning check. If the plan is lower or higher, the Program Director records why. The staffing plan never falls below what the IPs and health and safety needs require.

The plan is implemented through written schedules posted in advance, normally at least two weeks ahead. The Home Manager makes sure each shift has the number and mix of staff in the plan, with staff who know the residents' IPs and risk plans.

A person is placed on the schedule only after the Program Director confirms that the person is at least 18 years old, has a satisfactory criminal history check and registry review under ST-02, holds current First Aid and CPR certification with an in-person skills check, and has completed the pre-service training in ST-03 before independent duties. Staff who give medication must hold Medication Technician certification or be a licensed nurse (HW-01).
The staffing plan is also checked against each employee's three-month training under ST-04, so that a staff member is not assigned duties for which training is incomplete.

Services are available 24 hours a day, seven days a week. The Program Director maintains an on-call schedule listing the manager on call and a back-up staff member for every shift. Staff are given the on-call names and phone numbers in writing and at the home.

When a scheduled staff member calls out or cannot come, the Home Manager or on-call person fills the shift with a qualified employee, with float or relief staff, or with approved overtime. A staff member does not leave the home until a qualified replacement arrives. Staff are not left alone with residents unless the staffing plan allows it.

If a shift cannot be filled to the required level, the on-call manager reports to the Program Director immediately. The Program Director arranges additional coverage, assigns management staff to work the shift, and takes steps so that health and safety, medication administration and IP services are not compromised.

Staff supervise residents as the IP requires. Supervision levels, such as line-of-sight, within earshot, or periodic checks, are specified in the IP and communicated to all staff. Supervision is never used as a restriction without following IR-02.

At each shift change, outgoing staff give a documented handoff to incoming staff covering each resident's status, health concerns, medications, incidents, appointments, behavior concerns and pending tasks. The Home Manager reviews the handoff logs weekly.

For overnight shifts, the staff member remains on site, keeps phones and emergency contacts reachable, completes the required checks in the IP, and responds immediately to residents' calls. If the plan calls for awake staff, the staff member does not sleep. The Home Manager makes unannounced overnight visits at least [FREQUENCY] and records them.

Residents do not perform paid staff duties and are not counted in the staffing plan, as described in IR-10. Relatives, legal guardians and legally responsible persons are not paid to provide this service.

The Program Director reviews the staffing plan at least annually, and promptly after any admission, discharge, change in a resident's condition or IP, serious incident, surveyor finding, or complaint that suggests staffing is inadequate. Changes are recorded, dated and shared with the Home Manager and staff.

The Program Director reviews staffing data every quarter, including vacancies, overtime, call-outs, shifts staffed below plan, turnover, incidents linked to staffing, and resident or family concerns, and reports the results to the Governing Body under GOV-04. Corrective actions are assigned with due dates.
Staffing records are made available to DDA and OHCQ on request, and are used in surveys under GOV-09.

responsibilities.duty: Develops, approves and reviews the staffing plan; keeps the on-call schedule; makes sure staff are qualified; resolves coverage shortfalls; reports staffing data.
Implements the schedule; fills vacancies; supervises shift handoffs and overnight practice; reports staffing concerns.
Answers calls at any hour, provides back-up and emergency support, and arranges replacement staff.
Work the scheduled shifts, supervise as the IP requires, document handoffs, and stay until relieved.
Advises on health-related staffing needs, including medication coverage and nursing delegation.
Funds staffing at the level the plan requires and reviews quarterly staffing reports.

documentation: Written staffing plan for each home, with needs analysis and annual review
Documentation of overnight coverage decisions and IP updates
Posted staff schedules and records of actual staff worked
On-call and back-up schedule
Shift handoff logs
Records of shifts staffed below plan and corrective action
Staff qualification and training verification for each scheduled employee
Quarterly staffing reports to the Governing Body

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
policies.applies_to: All employees, contractors, consultants and volunteers of [AGENCY NAME] who have, or may have, direct contact with individuals served in the Community Living – Group Home program
policies.purpose: To protect individuals served by making sure [AGENCY NAME] does not employ or contract with anyone whose criminal history indicates behavior potentially harmful to individuals, and does not use anyone excluded from federal or State health care programs.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will not employ or contract with any person whose criminal history indicates behavior that is potentially harmful to individuals, as determined through a criminal history records check or background check (COMAR 10.22.02.11B; Health-General §19-1902 et seq.; COMAR 12.15.03). Every staff member, contractor and volunteer is checked before any direct contact with an individual. Results are recorded on the DDA Staff Criminal History form. Before direct contact and on a recurring basis afterward, every person is also screened against the OIG List of Excluded Individuals/Entities (LEIE) and the Maryland sanctioned provider list. A person who fails a check, or who is excluded or sanctioned, will not work with individuals, and the agency will not bill Medicaid for services that person delivers (42 USC 1320a-7). Fingerprint checks run through CJIS using the DDA agency authorization codes and the DDA instructions.

definitions.definition: A fingerprint-based check run through CJIS using DDA's agency authorization codes, following DDA instructions, to identify criminal history relevant to working with individuals with developmental disabilities.
Criminal history or conduct that, in the judgment of the Administrator after review under this policy, creates a risk to the health, safety, rights or property of individuals served.
The List of Excluded Individuals/Entities kept by the U.S. HHS Office of Inspector General. Excluded persons may not be paid from Medicaid funds (42 USC 1320a-7).
The State list of providers and individuals sanctioned or excluded from participation in Maryland Medicaid programs.
Any in-person interaction with an individual served, including unsupervised or supervised shadowing, orientation in the home, driving, or providing support.

procedures: The Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], designates a Background Check Coordinator and a back-up. The Coordinator manages all checks and keeps the tracking log.
Every job posting, contractor agreement and volunteer application states that employment or engagement depends on a satisfactory criminal history check and exclusion screening.

Before an offer becomes final, the applicant completes and signs the disclosure and consent forms for the criminal history records check. The applicant is told that false or missing information is grounds for withdrawal of the offer or termination.

The Coordinator submits the fingerprint-based check through CJIS using DDA's agency authorization codes and follows the current DDA instructions. The codes are kept in a restricted file and are not shared with applicants.
The Coordinator records the request date, the result and the decision on the DDA Staff Criminal History form and places the form in the personnel, contractor or volunteer file.
No person has any direct contact with an individual served until a result has been received, reviewed and recorded as acceptable. Pending results do not allow supervised shadowing in the home.

If a result shows criminal history, the Coordinator refers it to the Administrator within 1 business day. The Administrator reviews the nature of the offense, how recent it was, its relevance to the position and any behavior potentially harmful to individuals, and records the decision and reasons in writing.

If the Administrator finds the criminal history indicates behavior potentially harmful to individuals, the person is not hired, engaged or retained. The decision is documented and the person is notified in writing, consistent with applicable law.

Before direct contact, the Coordinator screens every applicant, contractor and volunteer against the OIG LEIE and the Maryland sanctioned provider list. The Coordinator prints or saves a dated screen shot or report of each result.
The Coordinator re-screens all current staff, contractors and volunteers against the OIG LEIE and the Maryland sanctioned provider list at least monthly, and records each date in the tracking log.

Any match is reported to the Administrator immediately. The person is removed from all duties involving individuals served until the match is resolved. Claims for services by an excluded person are not billed, and any prior billing is reviewed with the Compliance Officer under GOV-06.
Employees and volunteers must report to the Administrator within 1 business day any new arrest, charge or conviction. Failure to report is grounds for discipline up to termination.

The Administrator re-reviews the person's eligibility after any self-report or other notice of new criminal activity. The review is documented, and the person may be suspended from direct contact while it is pending.

The Coordinator reviews the tracking log quarterly to confirm that every active worker has a completed criminal history check and current exclusion screenings. Findings are reported to the Quality Assurance Committee under GOV-04.

Criminal history results are confidential. They are kept in a locked or access-restricted file separate from general personnel records and shared only with persons who need them to make employment decisions, or as required by DDA or OHCQ.

responsibilities.duty: Decides whether criminal history indicates behavior potentially harmful to individuals; approves all hiring, contracting and volunteer decisions; ensures the policy is implemented.
Submits CJIS checks, completes the DDA Staff Criminal History form, runs and records exclusion screenings, maintains the tracking log and restricted file.
Confirms that no person starts direct contact before results are recorded as acceptable.
Provide accurate information, sign consents and self-report new arrests, charges or convictions within 1 business day.

documentation: DDA Staff Criminal History form for each employee, contractor and volunteer
Signed disclosure and consent forms
Administrator's written review of any adverse or questionable result
Dated OIG LEIE and Maryland sanctioned provider list screening records, including monthly re-screens
Background check tracking log and quarterly review notes

policies.title: Direct Support Professional Orientation and Pre-Service Training
policies.applies_to: All direct support professionals, other staff and care providers who will carry out duties with individuals served by [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure every staff member and care provider is trained before working independently, so individuals receive safe, competent support.
policies.policy: Before performing any independent duties, every staff member and care provider of [AGENCY NAME] must receive adequate job training and complete DDA-approved training on seizure disorders, principles of behavior change, management of disruptive behaviors, medication administration, and the aging process. They must also complete blood-borne pathogens training in accordance with OSHA, 29 CFR 1910.1030 (COMAR 10.22.02.11C). Completion is documented on the DDA Staff Training form DD.APP.1.1. No staff member works unsupervised until the Program Director has signed off the pre-service training record.

definitions.definition: Any work with an individual served without a trained, qualified staff member present and directly supervising, including a solo shift, overnight coverage, medication administration, transportation or community outings.
Any person, whether an employee, contractor or agency worker, who delivers support to individuals served.
Training whose content and trainer meet DDA requirements for the topics listed in COMAR 10.22.02.11C.
The completed and signed DD.APP.1.1 and attached certificates, with the Program Director's sign-off that all required pre-service items are complete.
Orientation and skills training specific to the position, the home and the Individual Plans of the people supported, delivered and verified by a qualified trainer.

procedures: The Program Director, with the Training Coordinator, opens a DD.APP.1.1 training record for each new hire on the first day of employment, listing each required pre-service item and its date of completion.
Staff cannot be scheduled on any shift without a trained staff member present and directly supervising until the Program Director signs off the pre-service training record.

Orientation covers [AGENCY NAME]'s policies and procedures, the staff member's job description, the Individual Plan, health and safety needs and emergency procedures for each person served, and the home's emergency plan. The trainer and the new staff member sign and date the orientation record.

Job training includes shadowing an experienced, trained staff member, with a skills checklist covering personal care, mealtime and positioning supports, documentation and incident reporting. The trainer initials each item as demonstrated.
The staff member completes DDA-approved training on seizure disorders before independent duties. The date, trainer and hours are recorded on DD.APP.1.1 and the certificate is filed.
The staff member completes DDA-approved training on principles of behavior change before independent duties, and it is recorded on DD.APP.1.1.
The staff member completes DDA-approved training on management of disruptive behaviors before independent duties, and it is recorded on DD.APP.1.1.

The staff member completes DDA-approved training on medication administration before independent duties. Staff who will give medications must also meet the Medication Technician certification and delegating nurse requirements in HW-01 and HW-02. Pre-service training alone does not authorize medication administration.
The staff member completes DDA-approved training on the aging process before independent duties, and it is recorded on DD.APP.1.1.

Before independent duties, the staff member completes OSHA blood-borne pathogens training in accordance with 29 CFR 1910.1030, including exposure control, standard precautions and what to do after an exposure. See ST-05 for hepatitis B vaccination and post-exposure follow-up.

Before the first shift in each home, the staff member is trained on the individual-specific information for the people supported there, including health care needs, behavior plans, communication methods and any restrictions, and the trainer documents it.

When all items are complete, the Training Coordinator verifies that each entry on DD.APP.1.1 is dated and supported by a certificate or trainer signature. The Program Director then signs and dates the pre-service sign-off.
The Training Coordinator updates the training tracking log with the sign-off date, and the Shift Supervisor is informed that the staff member may be scheduled for independent duties.
If any required item is missing, expired or not verifiable, the staff member is removed from independent duties and works only under direct supervision until it is completed and recorded.

Contractors and agency staff who will provide direct support complete the same pre-service training, or the agency obtains and files equivalent documentation on DD.APP.1.1 before they work independently.
The Training Coordinator audits all pre-service records quarterly and reports findings to the Quality Assurance Committee under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures no staff member works independently before pre-service training is complete; signs off each training record.
Schedules DDA-approved training, maintains DD.APP.1.1 records and the tracking log, and runs quarterly audits.
Delivers and verifies job training and individual-specific training; never schedules an unqualified person on a solo shift.
Attend and complete all required training, sign documentation and ask for clarification when needed.
Provides resources for training and reviews audit results.

documentation: DD.APP.1.1 Staff Training Form for each staff member
Certificates or trainer verification for each DDA-approved topic and for blood-borne pathogens training
Orientation and job-skills checklist signed by trainer and staff member
Individual-specific training sign-in records
Program Director's signed pre-service sign-off
Training tracking log and quarterly audit reports

policies.title: Three-Month Training Requirements, CPR and First Aid
policies.applies_to: All direct support professionals and other staff and care providers of [AGENCY NAME] who provide support to individuals served
policies.purpose: To make sure all staff complete the DDA-required training within 3 months of hire and hold current First Aid and CPR certification with an in-person skills check, so they can respond to individuals' needs and emergencies.
policies.policy: Within 3 months of hire, every staff member and care provider of [AGENCY NAME] must complete DDA-approved training on: community integration and inclusion; individual-directed, outcome-oriented planning; the general characteristics and needs of the individuals served; First Aid and CPR (American Red Cross or equivalent); fundamental rights; communicable diseases; supporting choices; and communication skills (COMAR 10.22.02.11D). Under the Community Pathways Waiver standard for Community Living – Group Home, direct staff must be at least 18 years old and hold First Aid/CPR certification that includes an in-person skills check. Training is recorded on DD.APP.1.1. Online-only CPR courses without an in-person skills check do not meet this policy.

definitions.definition: The DDA-approved training listed in COMAR 10.22.02.11D that must be completed within 3 months after the date of hire.

definitions.term: First Aid/CPR with in-person skills check
definitions.definition: Certification from the American Red Cross or an equivalent provider that includes hands-on demonstration of skills in front of a qualified instructor.
The planning approach in which the individual, with the people he or she chooses, directs the outcomes and supports in the Individual Plan.
Practices that help individuals make informed decisions about their own lives, including the right to try new things and to make choices that staff may not share.
The first day the person is paid by, or begins work for, [AGENCY NAME] in any capacity.

procedures: On the date of hire, the Training Coordinator enters the staff member's 3-month completion deadline in the tracking log and on DD.APP.1.1.
The Training Coordinator schedules the staff member for DDA-approved training on community integration and inclusion, and records the date, trainer and hours when completed.
The Training Coordinator schedules training on individual-directed, outcome-oriented planning, and records completion on DD.APP.1.1.
The Training Coordinator schedules training on the general characteristics and needs of the individuals served, supplemented by individual-specific orientation to each person's Individual Plan.

The staff member completes First Aid and CPR training from the American Red Cross or an equivalent provider that includes an in-person skills check. The Training Coordinator keeps a copy of the card or certificate and records the expiration date.
Where possible, First Aid/CPR certification is scheduled in the first weeks of employment. The agency does not accept online-only courses lacking an in-person skills check.
The staff member completes training on fundamental rights and records it on DD.APP.1.1. It reinforces the rights policies in IR-01 and IR-02.
The staff member completes training on communicable diseases and records it on DD.APP.1.1. This training works together with ST-05 and HE-03.
The staff member completes training on supporting choices and records it on DD.APP.1.1.
The staff member completes training on communication skills, including supporting individuals who use alternative or augmentative communication, and records it on DD.APP.1.1.
At 30 days and again at 60 days after hire, the Training Coordinator reviews the staff member's record and notifies the Program Director and Shift Supervisor of any items still open.

If an item is not complete 14 days before the 3-month deadline, the Program Director arranges immediate scheduling. Any staff member who has not completed all items by the deadline is reported to the Administrator, and the Administrator decides on restrictions on duties until all items are done.

A staff member whose First Aid/CPR certification has lapsed may not work alone with individuals until recertification with an in-person skills check is complete. The Shift Supervisor ensures at least one currently certified staff member is on every shift.
The Training Coordinator checks First Aid/CPR expiration dates monthly and schedules recertification at least 60 days before expiration.
The Program Director signs and dates the 3-month completion section of DD.APP.1.1 when all items are verified.
The Training Coordinator audits 3-month training and CPR status across all staff quarterly and reports to the Quality Assurance Committee under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Sets deadlines, schedules training, tracks First Aid/CPR expirations and maintains DD.APP.1.1 records.
Verifies completion, handles overdue training, and ensures a certified staff member is on every shift.
Confirms certification status when scheduling and removes staff with lapsed certification from solo duties.
Complete all training within 3 months, keep CPR/First Aid current and provide certificates.
Decides on duty restrictions for overdue training and ensures resources are available.

documentation: DD.APP.1.1 Staff Training Form with the 3-month section completed and signed
First Aid/CPR card or certificate showing an in-person skills check and expiration date
Certificates or trainer sign-offs for each .11D topic
Training tracking log showing hire date, 3-month deadline and completion date
Monthly CPR expiration checks and quarterly audit reports

policies.title: Employee Health, Communicable Disease and TB Screening
policies.applies_to: All employees, contractors and volunteers of [AGENCY NAME] who have direct contact with individuals served
policies.purpose: To protect individuals and staff from communicable disease and bloodborne pathogen exposure through health screening, vaccination, exposure control and exclusion of ill staff.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains written infection control practices, including standard precautions (COMAR 10.22.02.10A(16)), and trains all staff on communicable diseases within 3 months of hire (COMAR 10.22.02.11D(6)). The agency sets pre-employment health screening and tuberculosis (TB) screening requirements by this policy, following the guidance of the local health department. The agency offers hepatitis B vaccination to covered employees under OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030 and provides bloodborne pathogens training before independent duties (COMAR 10.22.02.11C(3)). Staff who are ill with a condition that could be transmitted to individuals served are excluded from work until they are no longer a risk.

definitions.definition: An illness that can be passed from person to person, such as influenza, COVID-19, gastroenteritis, scabies, or tuberculosis.
Infection prevention practices applied to all individuals, including hand hygiene, gloves and other protective equipment, safe sharps handling and cleaning of surfaces.
Reasonably anticipated contact with blood or other potentially infectious materials during an employee's duties.
The written plan required by 29 CFR 1910.1030 that identifies tasks with exposure risk and describes protective measures, vaccination and post-exposure follow-up.
Removal of an employee from direct contact with individuals served until the employee is no longer able to transmit the condition.

procedures: The Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], designates an Infection Control Coordinator, who keeps the exposure control plan and employee health records.

After a conditional offer and before direct contact, each new employee, contractor and volunteer completes a health screening form and provides proof of TB screening as required by this policy, in line with local health department guidance. The Coordinator reviews and files the result.

If a screening is positive, the person is referred to a health care provider and the local health department, and is not assigned to direct contact until a licensed clinician documents that he or she is not contagious.
Health screening records are kept in a confidential medical file separate from the general personnel file, and are shared only with those who need to know.
The agency maintains a written exposure control plan and reviews it at least annually and when tasks or procedures change. Staff may review it at any time.

Employees with occupational exposure risk are offered the hepatitis B vaccine series at no cost, within 10 working days of initial assignment and after bloodborne pathogens training. An employee who declines signs a declination form and may change his or her mind later.
Before independent duties, each employee completes bloodborne pathogens training under 29 CFR 1910.1030. Training is repeated at least annually and recorded on DD.APP.1.1 or an equivalent record.
The agency provides gloves, gowns, masks, eye protection, hand hygiene supplies, sharps containers and spill kits in each home, and the Shift Supervisor checks supplies weekly.

Staff report to the Shift Supervisor before a shift if they have fever, vomiting, diarrhea, undiagnosed rash, a productive cough, conjunctivitis or another symptom that could indicate a communicable disease. They do not work until cleared under this policy.

The Shift Supervisor sends an ill staff member home, arranges coverage and informs the Program Director. Return to work follows the guidance of a health care provider or the local health department, and the Program Director records the return date.

After any needlestick, cut, splash or other exposure, the employee washes the area, notifies the Shift Supervisor immediately and receives a confidential medical evaluation as soon as possible. The Coordinator documents the incident and the source individual's follow-up as the law allows.
The Coordinator completes the exposure incident report within 24 hours and the Program Director reviews it for prevention. Related incidents involving individuals are handled under BH-05.
The Coordinator keeps a sharps injury log and reviews exposures with the Quality Assurance Committee.

When a communicable disease is identified in an individual or staff member, the Program Director consults the individual's health care provider or the local health department, follows reporting rules, notifies affected individuals' proponents as appropriate and applies the infection control measures in HE-03.
The Infection Control Coordinator reviews screening, vaccination and exposure records annually for all staff and reports gaps to the Administrator.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the exposure control plan, screening and vaccination records, and exposure follow-up; supervises supplies.
Enforces exclusion and return-to-work decisions and ensures coverage when staff are excluded.
Checks staff for symptoms at shift start, ensures supplies are stocked and starts exposure response.
Complete screening and training, use standard precautions, report symptoms and exposures promptly.
Funds vaccination and personal protective equipment and approves this policy.

documentation: Pre-employment health and TB screening records in the confidential medical file
Hepatitis B vaccination records or signed declination forms
Bloodborne pathogens training records
Exposure control plan and annual review record
Exposure incident reports and sharps injury log
Exclusion and return-to-work records

policies.title: Personnel Records and Job Descriptions
policies.applies_to: All positions at [AGENCY NAME] and all personnel files, including employees, contractors and volunteers who have direct contact with individuals
policies.purpose: To make sure every position has a written job description and every worker's file shows the qualifications, checks and training required before independent duties.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written job description for each position, which includes the nature and extent of training and experience required (COMAR 10.22.02.11E(1)). Each personnel file contains the criminal history check result, training documentation on DD.APP.1.1, licenses or certifications (such as Medication Technician and First Aid/CPR) and exclusion screening results. Training records must show that training was completed before independent duties (COMAR 10.22.02.11C). Personnel files are kept for at least 6 years after separation. Medical and criminal history records are kept confidential.

definitions.definition: A written statement of a position's duties, reporting relationships, and required training, experience, licenses and certifications.
The record for each worker containing hiring, qualification, training, supervision and employment documents.
A separate, restricted file holding health screening, vaccination, exposure and similar records.
Duties performed without a trained, qualified staff member present and directly supervising.

procedures: The Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], approves a written job description for every position, including Program Director, Shift Supervisor, direct support professional, Medication Technician, Training Coordinator and any contractor or volunteer role.

Each job description states the position's duties, supervisor, minimum age (at least 18 for direct staff), the nature and extent of training and experience required, and required licenses or certifications.
The Administrator reviews job descriptions at least annually and when duties change, and the review date is recorded on each description.
Each new hire receives a copy of the job description before starting. The employee signs an acknowledgment, which is filed in the personnel file.

The Human Resources designee opens a personnel file at hire containing: application and résumé, reference checks, signed job description, I-9 and tax forms, signed policy acknowledgment and signed confidentiality agreement.

The file includes the DDA Staff Criminal History form and result, and the OIG LEIE and Maryland sanctioned provider list screenings as required by ST-02. Criminal history details are kept in a restricted section.
The file contains DD.APP.1.1, with pre-service items (ST-03) and 3-month items (ST-04) dated, so that completion before independent duties can be verified.

The file contains copies of current licenses and certifications, including First Aid/CPR, Medication Technician certification (if applicable), driver's license and proof of insurance for staff who drive, with expiration dates tracked.
Health screening, TB screening, vaccination and exposure records are kept in the separate confidential medical file described in ST-05, not in the general personnel file.
The file includes supervision notes, performance evaluations, corrective action, commendations and any complaint or investigation outcome involving the worker.

The Human Resources designee audits each new file within 30 days of hire against a file checklist and corrects any gap. The Program Director confirms the worker has not started independent duties until the file shows required items are complete.
The Human Resources designee checks licenses, certifications and exclusion screening dates monthly and sends reminders at least 60 days before an expiration.

Personnel files are kept in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic system. Only the Administrator, Program Director, Human Resources designee and regulators acting within their authority may open them. Electronic files follow RC-02.

Personnel files are retained for at least 6 years after the worker's separation, or longer if required by law, an audit or a pending investigation or claim. Files are then destroyed by shredding or secure deletion, and the destruction is recorded.
On request by DDA, OHCQ or other regulator, the Administrator makes personnel files available promptly and logs the request.
The Quality Assurance Committee receives an annual personnel record audit summary under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Approves job descriptions, ensures qualifications are enforced and authorizes record release to regulators.
Creates and maintains personnel files, runs file audits and expiration checks, and handles retention and destruction.
Verifies that required items are complete before independent duties and keeps supervision records.
Provides current DD.APP.1.1 records and certificates for the file.
Provide accurate documents, sign acknowledgments and renew licenses and certifications on time.

documentation: Approved written job description for each position, with review dates
Signed job description acknowledgment for each worker
Personnel file checklist and 30-day file audit
DDA Staff Criminal History form, exclusion screenings, DD.APP.1.1 and licenses or certifications in each file
License and certification expiration tracking log
Record of record requests by regulators and of file destruction

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, care providers, contractors, consultants, volunteers and board members of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To protect individuals from exploitation and conflicts of interest and to set clear expectations for professional conduct.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] prohibits any financial or personal conflict of interest for staff, care providers and volunteers (COMAR 10.22.02.10A(13)). Relatives, legal guardians and legally responsible persons may not be paid to provide Community Living – Group Home services. Staff may not borrow from, or have financial dealings with, individuals served, and must follow the personal funds and property policy (IR-05). All staff must know and implement every policy as adopted (COMAR 10.22.02.10C).

definitions.definition: A situation in which a staff member's, care provider's or volunteer's financial or personal interest could influence, or appear to influence, decisions or actions affecting an individual served or the agency.
The limit that separates a respectful, supportive working relationship from personal, financial or exploitative involvement.
A person who has a legal duty to support the individual, such as a spouse or, for a minor, a parent.
Borrowing, lending, selling, buying, gifts of significant value, joint accounts, using an individual's property or accepting payment other than agency wages.

procedures: At hire, and in orientation, each staff member, contractor and volunteer receives this policy, signs an acknowledgment that he or she has read it and agrees to implement every [AGENCY NAME] policy, and the acknowledgment is filed under ST-06.

At hire and each January, every staff member, volunteer and board member completes a conflict of interest disclosure form listing financial interests, family relationships with individuals served, and outside employment that could conflict with duties.
The Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], reviews each disclosure within 10 business days, decides whether a conflict exists, and records the decision and any required safeguards or recusal.
Staff must disclose a new conflict to the Program Director within 2 business days of learning of it. Failure to disclose is grounds for discipline up to termination.

[AGENCY NAME] does not pay a relative, legal guardian or legally responsible person of an individual to provide Community Living – Group Home services. The Human Resources designee checks relationships against the individual's record before any hire.
Staff do not borrow money or property from, lend to, sell to, buy from or enter any other financial arrangement with an individual served or an individual's family.
Staff do not accept gifts of more than nominal value ($25 or less) from individuals or families. Any gift offered is reported to the Program Director and logged.

Staff are not named as a beneficiary, representative payee, agent under a power of attorney or guardian of an individual served while employed, unless the Administrator has reviewed and approved the situation in writing and it is lawful.

Staff handle individuals' money and property only as described in IR-05, with receipts, counts and two-person verification where required. Staff never use an individual's funds, card, food, phone, vehicle or belongings for personal purposes.

Staff keep relationships with individuals professional. They do not engage in romantic or sexual relationships with individuals, share personal social media connections or private contact information, or take individuals to their own homes outside of agency-approved activities.
Staff do not perform personal errands or work for an individual served outside their agency duties for pay, and do not ask individuals to do paid staff tasks (see IR-10).
Staff respect individuals' rights and privacy and use the grievance and reporting processes in IR-03, BH-04 and BH-05 for any concerns.

Staff report any suspected boundary violation, exploitation or conflict of interest immediately to the Program Director, or to the Administrator if the report concerns the Program Director. Reports of suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation follow BH-04 and BH-05. Retaliation against any person who reports is prohibited.

The Administrator investigates boundary and conflict reports promptly. Substantiated violations lead to corrective action up to termination, and any required reports are made to DDA or OHCQ under RC-03.
The Program Director reviews conduct expectations in staff meetings at least twice a year, and the Quality Assurance Committee reviews disclosures and boundary reports annually under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Reviews disclosures, decides on conflicts, investigates reports and imposes corrective action.
Receives staff reports, monitors boundaries in the homes and reinforces expectations in supervision and meetings.
Collects acknowledgments and disclosures, and screens for relatives, guardians and legally responsible persons before hire.

responsibilities.role: All staff, care providers and volunteers
responsibilities.duty: Follow this policy and every agency policy, disclose conflicts, avoid financial dealings with individuals and report concerns.

documentation: Signed policy acknowledgment for each worker
Annual conflict of interest disclosure forms and the Administrator's review notes
Gift log
Reports and investigations of boundary or conflict concerns, and resulting corrective action
Staff meeting records showing conduct review
Annual Quality Assurance Committee review summary

policies.title: Employment Nondiscrimination
policies.applies_to: All applicants, employees, contracted staff and volunteers of [AGENCY NAME]; all hiring, promotion, discipline and termination decisions
policies.purpose: To prevent discrimination in employment, as required by COMAR 10.22.02.11, and to make sure every employment decision is based on job-related qualifications and on the health and safety needs of the individuals we support.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not discriminate in recruitment, hiring, assignment, pay, training, promotion, discipline or termination on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran status or any other characteristic protected by federal or Maryland law. Each position has a written job description that lists essential duties and qualifications, as required by COMAR 10.22.02.11. Employment decisions are made by reference to that description. The agency provides reasonable accommodation to qualified applicants and employees with disabilities and for religious practice, unless doing so would cause undue hardship. Criminal history is considered only as COMAR 10.22.02.11 requires, to exclude anyone whose history indicates behavior potentially harmful to individuals. It is never used as a pretext for discrimination. Retaliation against anyone who raises a discrimination concern or takes part in an investigation is prohibited.

definitions.definition: A characteristic on which federal or Maryland law prohibits employment decisions, including race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability and the others listed in this policy.

A change to the application process, job duties, schedule or work environment that lets a qualified person with a disability, or a person with a sincere religious practice, apply for or perform a job, unless it causes undue hardship.
A fundamental duty of a position, as listed in the written job description.

procedures: The Program Director, with [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], maintains a written job description for every position before it is advertised. It states essential duties, required qualifications, training requirements and physical demands (see ST-06).
Job postings and applications use only job-related criteria taken from the job description. They include the statement: '[AGENCY NAME] is an equal opportunity employer.'

Interviewers use the same core questions for all candidates for a position. They do not ask about protected characteristics, pregnancy or family plans, or about medical conditions or disability before a conditional offer.
Interviewers record job-related, objective notes for each candidate on the interview form. The forms are kept with the hiring file.

A conditional offer is made only after interview and reference review. Criminal history and registry checks follow ST-02. Any decision to exclude based on criminal history is reviewed and approved in writing by [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], who documents how the history indicates potentially harmful behavior toward individuals.

Medical or fitness inquiries are made only after a conditional offer and only for requirements that apply to everyone in the job category (see ST-05). Medical information is kept in a separate confidential file.

An applicant or employee may request an accommodation orally or in writing to the Program Director or [ADMINISTRATOR NAME]. A decision is made after an interactive discussion with the person and is documented within 10 business days of the request, or sooner if the need is urgent.

Pay, schedule, assignment, training and promotion decisions are based on the job description, performance and agency needs. The decision-maker writes down the reason for any promotion, demotion or disciplinary action.
Progressive discipline and termination follow the Personnel Records process in ST-06. [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] reviews each termination to confirm it rests on documented, job-related reasons.

An employee who believes they have been discriminated against or harassed may report it to the Program Director, to [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], or to a governing body member if the report concerns either of them. Reports may be oral or written.

The person receiving a report notifies [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] the same business day. The agency begins a prompt, impartial investigation within 5 business days and interviews the parties and witnesses. A written finding and any corrective action are completed and shared with the complainant.

Anyone who retaliates against a person who made a good-faith report is subject to discipline up to termination. Complainants are checked on at 30 and 90 days after the finding to confirm no retaliation has occurred.

All employees review this policy at hire and at each annual policy refresh, and sign the acknowledgment in their personnel file (see GOV-03). Supervisors receive additional guidance on lawful interviewing, accommodation and anti-retaliation.

The standing committee or governing body reviews a summary of discrimination complaints and outcomes, with no identifying detail beyond what is needed, as part of the annual quality assurance review (see GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Adopts this policy and ensures the agency complies with employment nondiscrimination law.
Maintains job descriptions, approves exclusion decisions, decides accommodation requests, and oversees investigations.
Applies this policy in hiring and supervision, receives reports, and trains supervisors.
Treat co-workers and applicants without discrimination, report concerns, and do not retaliate.

documentation: Written job descriptions for each position
Interview notes and hiring decision records
Accommodation requests and decisions
Discrimination complaint and investigation files, kept separate from personnel files
Signed employee policy acknowledgments
Annual summary of complaints and outcomes for QA review

policies.title: Wage, Hour and Leave Compliance
policies.applies_to: All employees of [AGENCY NAME], including hourly direct support staff, overnight staff and exempt administrative staff
policies.purpose: To pay every employee at least the minimum wage that applies where they work, pay overtime correctly, count all hours worked, and provide earned sick and safe leave and paid family and medical leave contributions as Maryland law requires.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] pays no employee less than the highest applicable federal, State of Maryland or local minimum wage. The State minimum is $15.00 per hour. Local rates in effect as of July 1, 2026 are: Montgomery County $18.00 for employers with 51 or more employees, $16.50 for employers with 11 to 50 employees (and for certain nonprofit and Medicaid-funded home care providers), and $15.95 for employers with 10 or fewer employees; Howard County $16.00; and Prince George's County $15.30. Non-exempt employees are paid overtime under the Fair Labor Standards Act (29 USC 206-207) for hours over 40 in a workweek, and paid training time is treated as hours worked. Employees accrue earned sick and safe leave at 1 hour for every 30 hours worked, up to 40 hours per year, under Md. Code, Labor & Employment §3-1304. The leave is paid when the agency has 15 or more employees. Beginning January 1, 2027, the agency withholds and remits Maryland FAMLI contributions at 0.9% of wages, split 0.45% employer and 0.45% employee, except that an employer with fewer than 15 employees remits only the employee share. The agency does not allow off-the-clock work.

definitions.definition: All time an employee is required or permitted to work, including paid training, required meetings, travel between work sites during the shift, and time spent on required documentation.
An employee entitled to minimum wage and overtime under the FLSA.
Leave employees accrue at 1 hour per 30 hours worked, up to 40 hours per year, for the purposes allowed by Md. Code, Labor & Employment §3-1304.
The Maryland Family and Medical Leave Insurance program, funded by wage-based contributions beginning January 1, 2027.

procedures: Before the first hire at each site, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] identifies the county where the site is located and the applicable State and local minimum wage. The agency's head count is then used to determine the applicable Montgomery County tier, if relevant. The determination is recorded in the payroll file.

Payroll compares every pay rate to the highest applicable minimum wage. This check is repeated each January 1 and each July 1, and whenever a State or local rate changes or the agency's employee count moves across a tier threshold. Rate changes are made effective on the date the new rate applies.

Each employee is classified as exempt or non-exempt at hire based on actual duties and salary, and the classification is recorded in the personnel file. Direct support staff are treated as non-exempt hourly employees.

Employees record time by the timekeeping system at the start and end of each shift. Supervisors review and approve timesheets each pay period. Employees may not perform work off the clock, and any unrecorded time that is reported is paid.

Paid pre-service orientation, required training, mandatory staff meetings, and certification classes that the agency requires are recorded as hours worked and paid at no less than the applicable minimum wage (see ST-03 and ST-04).

Overtime is calculated per workweek on all hours worked over 40 at one and one-half times the regular rate. The regular rate includes shift differentials and non-discretionary bonuses. Overtime must be approved by the Program Director in advance when possible, but is paid whether or not it was approved.

The Program Director schedules staff to meet the staffing plan in ST-01 while controlling overtime. Awake overnight shifts and any on-call or sleep-time arrangements are reviewed by [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] with qualified payroll or legal advice before they are used. Only time that meets legal standards is excluded from hours worked.

Payroll sets up earned sick and safe leave accrual for every employee from the first day of work: 1 hour for every 30 hours worked, up to 40 hours accrued per year. Each pay stub or portal shows the current balance.

When the agency has 15 or more employees, earned sick and safe leave is paid at the employee's regular rate. If the agency has fewer than 15 employees, the agency provides the leave in the manner Md. Code, Labor & Employment §3-1304 requires for that size of employer. [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] re-counts employees at least each January and documents the result.

An employee requests leave orally or in writing, as far in advance as practicable. The Program Director approves it and arranges coverage under ST-01. Leave is not denied for a permitted purpose and is not counted against the employee in attendance or discipline.

The agency registers for FAMLI before January 1, 2027, and sets up payroll to withhold 0.45% of wages from each employee and to remit the employer share of 0.45%, unless the agency has fewer than 15 employees, in which case only the employee share is remitted. [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] confirms the employee count and remittance obligation each year.

Each pay period the agency issues a wage statement showing hours worked, rate, overtime, deductions and the leave balance. Wages are paid on a regular schedule at least as often as Maryland law requires. Deductions are made only when allowed by law or authorized in writing by the employee.

An employee who believes they have been underpaid, or who was not given leave, reports it to the Program Director or [ADMINISTRATOR NAME]. The agency reviews it within 5 business days and pays any amount owed on the next payroll, or sooner. No retaliation is permitted.

[ADMINISTRATOR NAME] reviews a payroll audit sample (minimum wage, overtime, leave balances, training time) at least quarterly and reports exceptions to the governing body. Required wage, hour and leave postings are displayed at each site and at the office.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures the budget supports lawful wages, overtime, leave and FAMLI contributions.
Determines applicable wage rates, employee classifications and employer size thresholds, and oversees quarterly audits.
Approves timesheets and leave, schedules to limit overtime, and prevents off-the-clock work.
Calculates pay, overtime, leave accruals and FAMLI contributions, and issues wage statements.
Record all time worked accurately and report pay or leave problems.
